functions.funcDef: Provide the control authority to position the aircraft about all three axes across the flight envelope including the engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Position roll (ailerons/spoilers), pitch (stabiliser/elevators) and yaw (split rudder) surfaces in response to pilot and autopilot commands; SDD §5.3.2 shows each axis on independent actuation/hydraulic supply.

functions.funcDef: Provide the control authority to position the aircraft about all three axes across the flight envelope including the engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Extend/retract Fowler flaps and leading-edge slats for take-off and landing; SDD §5.3.2 shows two independent power drive units on a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes.

functions.funcDef: Provide the control authority to position the aircraft about all three axes across the flight envelope including the engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Compute and enforce envelope protection in the normal control law, annunciating degraded laws; SDD §5.3.2/§5.3.6 shows three dissimilar voting computers.

functions.funcDef: Provide thrust for all phases of flight from four podded turbofans, with the directional-control case set by outboard-engine asymmetry (SDD §5.1.1, §5.1.3).
functions.subDef: Generate and control thrust from four turbofans via autothrottle and FADEC, protecting against overspeed/overtemperature; SDD §5.1.6 shows FADEC dual channels on independent feeds per engine.

functions.funcDef: Provide thrust for all phases of flight from four podded turbofans, with the directional-control case set by outboard-engine asymmetry (SDD §5.1.1, §5.1.3).
functions.subName: Provide reverse thrust for ground deceleration
functions.subDef: Deploy inboard-engine thrust reversers on the ground, inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement with a mechanical sleeve lock (SDD §5.1.2).

functions.funcName: Decelerate and control the aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads on semi-prepared surfaces, provide braking and directional control, and meet the 1,800 m landing requirement (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Provide carbon multi-disc braking with anti-skid, normally from hydraulic B and alternately A with accumulator reserve; SDD §5.6.2 shows dual hydraulic supply and per-wheel-pair anti-skid.

functions.funcName: Decelerate and control the aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads on semi-prepared surfaces, provide braking and directional control, and meet the 1,800 m landing requirement (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Provide hydraulic nose-wheel steering commanded from tillers and rudder pedals, with a mechanical disconnect for towing (SDD §5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Decelerate and control the aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads on semi-prepared surfaces, provide braking and directional control, and meet the 1,800 m landing requirement (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Support the aircraft and absorb ground loads
functions.subDef: Extend/retract the gear and support/spread footprint on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces via one nose unit and six main bogies, with free-fall alternate extension and dual downlock sensing (SDD §5.6.2).

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting that tells the crew what has failed (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Drive display units/HUDs from three display processors on dual networks, fed by three air-data inertial reference units; SDD §5.11.2/§5.11.3 shows the redundancy set.

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting that tells the crew what has failed (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Consolidate every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with procedures, driven by two independent processing channels (SDD §5.11.2).

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting that tells the crew what has failed (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Provide standby attitude, airspeed and altitude from an integrated standby instrument sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays (SDD §5.11.2/§5.11.3).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold and control the pressure differential across the fuselage (SDD §5.9.1).
functions.subName: Condition and pressurise flight deck and hold
functions.subDef: Supply conditioned air from two packs and control differential via two controllers/outflow valves with pneumatic backup and independent mechanical relief; flight deck and hold are separate conditioning zones (SDD §5.9.2).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold and control the pressure differential across the fuselage (SDD §5.9.1).
functions.subName: Close, lock and monitor the nose pressure boundary
functions.subDef: Drive twelve latches and eight lock pins closed, confirm lock via dual dissimilar sensing, and enforce the residual-differential interlock before unlock; SDD §5.7 (structural load path itself is treated as structure per §5.7.3, not a function).

functions.funcName: Protect the aircraft from ice accretion
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes where accretion would be unacceptable, for flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Anti-ice airframe surfaces and engine inlets
functions.subDef: Protect wing leading edges and inlet cowls by bleed air, and stabiliser leading edges by six independently controlled electric zones (SDD §5.10.2).

functions.funcName: Protect the aircraft from ice accretion
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes where accretion would be unacceptable, for flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subDef: Electrically heat probes, static ports, windshields and the two ice detectors, each monitored individually (SDD §5.10.2).

functions.funcName: Protect the aircraft from ice accretion
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes where accretion would be unacceptable, for flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subDef: Detect ice via two detectors on opposite sides of the forward fuselage, commanding automatic activation and providing advisory to the crew (SDD §5.10.2).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected, and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them (SDD §5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Provide dual-loop continuous fire detection per engine nacelle and APU compartment with AND logic degrading to single loop, plus overheat detection on bleed ducts and gear bays and smoke detection at nine hold stations (SDD §5.12.2).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected, and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them (SDD §5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Discharge two cross-plumbed bottles per engine pair on crew command and discharge the dedicated APU bottle automatically when unattended (SDD §5.12.2).

functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade of up to 72.6 t along the full hold length and maintain that restraint through all flight and ground load cases (SDD §5.8.1).
functions.subName: Restrain and tension the payload longitudinally
functions.subDef: Provide longitudinal restraint by two tension straps per saddle, tensioned by electric winches and mechanically locked, with load paths sized so loss of any one strap is carried by neighbours; hold floor hard points themselves are structure per §5.8.3 (SDD §5.8.2).

functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade of up to 72.6 t along the full hold length and maintain that restraint through all flight and ground load cases (SDD §5.8.1).
functions.subDef: Instrument every strap continuously via a single tension loop, annunciating loss of tension on any strap and a restraint condition on two adjacent stations (SDD §5.8.2).

functions.funcDef: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events, and for the descent and diversion that follow (SDD §5.13.1).
functions.subDef: Supply oxygen from two high-pressure cylinders on a common manifold with crossover to four quick-donning masks with independent regulators, sized for four occupants for the diversion time with reserve (SDD §5.13.2).

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous surface response to crew pitch command
fha.effAc: Primary pitch surface responds erroneously relative to the crew pitch command, producing an uncommanded pitch excursion and departure from the intended flight path; if large or outside the manoeuvre envelope the aircraft can exceed structural or aerodynamic limits with loss of flight-path control.
fha.effCrew: Crew face an erroneous pitch response to their own input; recovery difficulty depends on magnitude and phase and may exceed available authority near the ground.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED: erroneous primary pitch response is a plausible path to loss of flight-path control, which for a transport aircraft is Catastrophic (Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh). Magnitude/authority and MAC boundary not stated in the function definition — confirm the worst-case pitch excursion and any envelope-protection limiting before fixing the class. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch surface motion with no command
fha.effAc: Primary pitch surface moves with no crew command, producing an uncommanded pitch excursion and departure from the intended flight path; a hardover or sustained runaway can exceed structural or aerodynamic limits and lead to loss of flight-path control.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect an uncommanded pitch motion and counter it; recovery difficulty depends on rate, magnitude and phase and may exceed available authority near the ground.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED: uncommanded primary pitch motion is a plausible path to loss of flight-path control (Catastrophic ↔ Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh). Rate/magnitude of the uncommanded motion and any monitor/limiting are not in the function definition — confirm worst-case before fixing the class. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous surface response to crew roll command
fha.effAc: Primary roll surface responds erroneously relative to the crew roll command, producing an uncommanded roll/bank excursion and departure from the intended flight path; if large or asymmetric the aircraft can exceed bank/structural limits with loss of flight-path control.
fha.effCrew: Crew face an erroneous roll response to their own input; recovery difficulty depends on magnitude and phase and may exceed available authority near the ground.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED: erroneous primary roll response is a plausible path to loss of flight-path control (Catastrophic ↔ Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh). Magnitude/authority not stated in the function definition — confirm worst-case roll excursion before fixing the class. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded roll surface motion with no command
fha.effAc: Primary roll surface moves with no crew command, producing an uncommanded roll/bank excursion and departure from the intended flight path; a hardover or sustained runaway can exceed bank/structural limits and lead to loss of flight-path control.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect an uncommanded roll motion and counter it; recovery difficulty depends on rate, magnitude and phase and may exceed available authority near the ground.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED: uncommanded primary roll motion is a plausible path to loss of flight-path control (Catastrophic ↔ Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh). Rate/magnitude and any monitor are not in the function definition — confirm worst-case before fixing the class. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous surface response to crew yaw command
fha.effAc: Primary yaw surface (rudder) responds erroneously relative to the crew yaw command, producing an uncommanded sideslip/yaw excursion; if large this loads the vertical tail and structure and can lead to loss of directional/flight-path control, and interacts with the sizing directional-control case.
fha.effCrew: Crew face an erroneous yaw response to their own input; recovery difficulty depends on magnitude and phase and may exceed available authority.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED: erroneous primary yaw response is a plausible path to loss of directional/flight-path control and vertical-tail overload (Catastrophic ↔ Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh). Rudder is split upper/lower with independent supplies (SDD §5.3.2); whether an erroneous response is limited to one segment materially affects the effect and class — confirm worst-case authority before fixing. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded yaw surface motion with no crew command
fha.effAc: Uncommanded rudder deflection introduces an unintended yaw/sideslip; on a four-engine high-wing freighter this excites Dutch-roll and roll coupling and, at the split-rudder authority available, can exceed sideslip and structural side-load limits if the deflection is large or hard-over.
fha.effCrew: Crew perceive the yaw excursion, must counter with pedal and possibly identify/isolate the affected rudder segment; increased workload during a dynamic upset.
fha.effPax: None — hold is unoccupied in flight, crew-only complement.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The function definition and SDD establish an uncommanded yaw excursion but do not establish the MAGNITUDE/rate of the uncommanded motion (small nuisance deflection vs. hard-over) nor the resulting sideslip/structural margin, and the split-rudder segments limit the authority any single supply commands. Severity spans Major to Hazardous depending on deflection magnitude and controllability — cannot be derived from the function alone; requires the surface authority/rate and controllability assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Primary surface jam restricting available control authority
fha.effAc: A jammed primary surface reduces or removes control authority about the affected axis; remaining authority (dual actuation per surface, mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim and lower rudder) may permit continued controlled flight but the effect depends on which surface/axis jams and at what deflection.
fha.effCrew: Crew must diagnose the jam, revert to available control paths and manage a degraded-control landing; elevated workload, potentially a mechanical-reversion approach.
fha.effPax: None — hold is unoccupied in flight, crew-only complement.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The function establishes that authority is restricted, but severity depends on WHICH surface jams, at what deflection, and how much authority remains via the second actuator and the mechanical reversion path — a jam at neutral is far less severe than a hard-over jam. Not derivable from the function definition alone; needs the per-surface residual-authority/controllability assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded pitch surface drift below crew detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: A slow uncommanded pitch-surface drift below the detection threshold produces a gradual, un-annunciated trim/attitude change; with the crew unaware and taking no action the effect depends on whether envelope protection arrests the drift or it accumulates toward an out-of-trim / attitude excursion.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware by definition and continue normal duties, taking no corrective action; awareness would only arise if the drift eventually produces a perceptible attitude or performance change.
fha.effPax: None — hold is unoccupied in flight, crew-only complement.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware condition: the aircraft outcome cannot be derived from the function definition alone, because whether the slow pitch drift is arrested by flight-envelope protection (SF-003) or accumulates to an attitude/trim excursion determines the severity, and that interaction is not established here. Left empty pending the drift-accumulation / protection-coverage assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded roll surface drift below crew detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: A slow uncommanded roll-surface (aileron/spoiler) drift below the detection threshold produces a gradual, un-annunciated roll/bank tendency; with the crew unaware and taking no action the outcome depends on whether protection arrests the drift or it accumulates toward a bank excursion.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware by definition and continue normal duties, taking no corrective action; awareness would only arise if the drift eventually produces a perceptible bank or heading change.
fha.effPax: None — hold is unoccupied in flight, crew-only complement.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware condition: severity depends on whether slow roll drift is arrested by flight-envelope protection or accumulates to a bank excursion — an interaction not established by the SF-001 definition. Left empty pending the drift-accumulation / protection-coverage assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded yaw surface drift below crew detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: A slow uncommanded rudder-segment drift below the detection threshold produces a gradual, un-annunciated sideslip/yaw tendency; with the crew unaware and taking no action the outcome depends on whether protection or trim compensation masks it or it accumulates toward a sideslip excursion.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware by definition and continue normal duties, taking no corrective action; awareness would only arise if the drift eventually produces a perceptible yaw, sideslip or lateral-trim change.
fha.effPax: None — hold is unoccupied in flight, crew-only complement.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware condition: severity depends on whether slow yaw drift is masked/arrested or accumulates to a sideslip excursion, and on the split-rudder authority involved — an interaction not established by the SF-001 definition. Left empty pending the drift-accumulation / controllability assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pitch control authority — reduced pitch authority or increased difficulty controlling the pitch axis, function still performed by remaining means
fha.effAc: Reduced pitch control authority; aircraft controllable in pitch by remaining actuation but with degraded manoeuvre/trim capability. Elevators are driven from two hydraulic systems (A and C) with mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim, so a partial loss leaves a survivable but degraded pitch capability.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to maintain pitch attitude and trim; degraded-law condition annunciated where FCS control law degrades.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold not occupied in flight; crew-only aircraft.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects are a significant reduction in pitch capability and a significant increase in crew workload, with control retained via redundant actuation and mechanical reversion — consistent with Major. PROPOSED: whether a partial pitch loss can be bounded above Hazardous depends on the worst-case authority remaining and flight phase, which is a controllability substantiation not closable from the SDD; confirm against FCS sizing. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of roll control authority — reduced roll authority or increased difficulty controlling the roll axis, function still performed by remaining means
fha.effAc: Reduced roll control authority; aircraft controllable in roll by remaining ailerons/spoilers but with degraded roll rate and manoeuvre capability. Ailerons are supplied from two hydraulic systems (B and C) and roll is also achieved by multi-function spoilers, so a partial loss retains roll capability.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to maintain wings level and control lateral flight path; degraded-law condition annunciated where FCS control law degrades.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold not occupied in flight; crew-only aircraft.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects are a significant reduction in roll capability with control retained via redundant aileron supplies and spoilers — consistent with Major. PROPOSED: worst-case remaining roll authority, especially in the blade-loaded / crosswind landing case, is a controllability substantiation not closable from the SDD; confirm against FCS sizing. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of yaw control authority — reduced yaw authority or increased difficulty controlling the yaw axis, function still performed by remaining means
fha.effAc: Reduced yaw control authority; aircraft controllable in yaw by the remaining rudder segment. Rudder is split into upper and lower segments on hydraulic systems A and B respectively; loss of one supply leaves the other segment. The sizing case is an outboard engine failure at V1 at maximum blade payload, which sets the split-segment arrangement so a single rudder supply loss still leaves sufficient authority.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to maintain directional control, most demanding coincident with asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm; degraded-law condition annunciated where applicable.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold not occupied in flight; crew-only aircraft.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the SDD alone: the directional-control sizing case is an outboard engine-out at V1 at maximum blade payload, and whether a partial yaw-authority loss coincident with that asymmetric-thrust case leaves adequate controllability (Major) or is a controllability-limiting condition (Hazardous) is a controllability substantiation not derivable from the design description. Confirm severity against FCS/rudder authority analysis for the sizing case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of primary flight-path control about all axes — the aircraft cannot be controlled about pitch, roll and yaw by any means
fha.effAc: Loss of control of the aircraft trajectory about all axes; no means remains to control the flight path. Mechanical reversion exists only to stabiliser trim and the lower rudder segment, which is a survivable-but-degraded means for a subset of axes, not full primary control — complete loss about all axes leaves no controllable flight path.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to control the aircraft; excessive workload beyond capability.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold not occupied in flight; crew-only aircraft.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of primary flight-path control about all axes results in an uncontrolled trajectory — a loss-of-control condition preventing continued safe flight and landing, classified Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1×10^-9/fh). Derived from the stated effect; confirm the mechanical-reversion scope does not partially mitigate the all-axes case. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment across span — high-lift devices deploy asymmetrically across the wing span, producing an uncommanded rolling moment
fha.effAc: Uncommanded rolling moment from asymmetric high-lift across a 160 m span, occurring in the low-speed take-off/approach/landing regime. High-lift comprises Fowler flaps in four sections and full-span slats on a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section, so asymmetry is intended to be arrested; the residual asymmetry that defeats the brakes produces a roll upset requiring corrective roll authority.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to counter the rolling moment with roll control while low and slow; asymmetry/jam discretes provided to the crew.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold not occupied in flight; crew-only aircraft.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded rolling moment in the low-speed regime with reduced margins is a controllability condition; on a 160 m span the rolling moment from span-wise asymmetry can be large, supporting Hazardous (↔ Extremely Remote, 1×10^-7/fh) pending confirmation. PROPOSED: the actual severity depends on the maximum asymmetry the section asymmetry brakes permit and the roll authority available to counter it at approach speed — a controllability substantiation not closable from the SDD. Confirm against high-lift asymmetry and roll-authority analysis; a worse-case unarrested asymmetry could drive Catastrophic. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift movement with no command
fha.effAc: Uncommanded change in high-lift configuration alters lift, drag and pitch trim without crew command; if asymmetric across span it produces a rolling/yawing moment. Effect is most severe at low speed / high angle of attack near the flap or slat placard where an uncommanded change moves the aircraft toward a stall or overspeed condition.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the unexpected configuration change and counter the resulting trim/roll excursion while diagnosing; increased workload at a critical phase.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction is grounded (uncommanded config change → trim/roll excursion; asymmetry brakes fitted per section), but the SDD does not state the resulting handling margin, whether asymmetry brakes arrest the movement before it becomes uncontrollable, or the speed/attitude excursion magnitude. Cannot derive Hazardous vs Catastrophic vs Major without that outcome. Severity left blank pending the controllability/asymmetry-arrest analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous high-lift position relative to command
fha.effAc: High-lift surfaces attain a position different from that commanded, so the achieved lift/drag differs from that assumed for the phase; a shortfall at take-off or landing degrades performance against the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement and the take-off configuration, and an asymmetric error produces a rolling/yawing moment.
fha.effCrew: Crew acts on displayed/expected configuration that does not match the actual surface position; incorrect speed schedule or configuration flown until detected.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Grounded that achieved config diverges from commanded (performance/asymmetry consequence), but the SDD does not quantify the position error, whether it is symmetric or asymmetric, or the residual controllability. Without the excursion magnitude and controllability outcome the class cannot be derived. Left blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous high-lift position indication with actual mismatch
fha.effAc: Indicated high-lift position disagrees with actual surface position; the crew and the take-off configuration / performance computation use a false configuration, so speeds and distances are computed for a configuration the aircraft is not in. The aircraft handling matches the true (unannunciated) configuration.
fha.effCrew: Crew is unaware of the true configuration and takes no corrective action; may set an incorrect speed schedule or accept an invalid take-off configuration based on misleading indication.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Misleading-indication path is grounded (position feeds performance computation and take-off configuration monitor), but the aircraft-level outcome depends on the size of the actual mismatch and whether the take-off configuration monitor still trips on the true state — neither is stated. Cannot classify without the outcome of an uncorrected mismatch. Left blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded high-lift extension within available authority
fha.effAc: High-lift is still extended but to a reduced degree within available authority, giving a higher approach/landing and lift-off speed and a longer required distance; against a 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement with ~1,080 m predicted rollout the erosion of that margin is the effect of interest.
fha.effCrew: Crew flies an amended (higher-speed) schedule for the achieved configuration; increased approach speed and workload, manageable with annunciation.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is grounded as a performance/margin reduction against the stated landing requirement, but the SDD does not state how much authority is lost, the resulting speed increase, or whether the remaining margin to 1,800 m is preserved. Whether this is Minor or Major depends on that margin, which is not given. Left blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: High-lift retracted or jammed at intermediate position
fha.effAc: High-lift jams or remains retracted, so no or minimal high-lift is available for take-off and landing; stall, lift-off and approach speeds rise substantially and the required field length increases, eroding or exceeding the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement. A jam during transit may leave the surfaces asymmetric, adding a rolling/yawing moment.
fha.effCrew: Crew must fly a flapless/reduced-flap approach and landing at elevated speeds and re-plan the field, with elevated workload; asymmetry brakes are intended to hold the jam symmetric.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Grounded as loss of high-lift for take-off/landing with a distance and speed penalty, but the SDD gives no flapless performance data, no resulting field length against the 1,800 m requirement, and no controllability outcome for an asymmetric jam. Class (Major vs Hazardous) cannot be derived without that performance/controllability result. Left blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of high-lift configuration capability (flaps and slats cannot be extended by any means)
fha.effAc: Aircraft must take off and land in a clean or last-attained configuration; stall and approach speeds elevated, landing distance grows against a fixed 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement (predicted rollout ~1,080 m at MLW).
fha.effCrew: Crew fly a high-speed, non-standard approach with reduced margins; increased workload managing energy and landing distance on a semi-prepared strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Elevated approach/landing speeds and degraded landing performance against a marginal semi-prepared landing distance produce a large reduction in safety margins and higher crew workload — consistent with Hazardous. Confirm against the actual clean-configuration landing performance and whether the 1,080 m/1,800 m margin is retained without high-lift; if margin is lost outright the effect may approach Catastrophic. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Envelope protection activates without a valid exceedance (spurious/nuisance intervention)
fha.effAc: Protection intervenes against a non-existent exceedance, potentially opposing the crew's intended flight path in a phase where authority intervention is unexpected.
fha.effCrew: Crew face an uncommanded control input contrary to intent; must recognise, override or revert law, with workload and startle depending on phase and transient magnitude.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the provided material: the SDD states envelope protection is active in the normal law and that degraded laws are annunciated, but does not describe the authority, transient magnitude, phase-dependence or recoverability of a spurious protection activation. Effect on aircraft trajectory (nuisance nudge vs. sustained hard-over near the ground) cannot be grounded, so severity is left blank pending that characterisation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Envelope protection fails to inhibit an actual exceedance (protection does not act when the envelope is exceeded)
fha.effAc: Aircraft is permitted to depart the intended flight envelope (e.g. stall, overspeed, load-factor or attitude exceedance) with no protective intervention, risking loss of control or structural exceedance.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the exceedance and recover manually without the assumed protection safety net; recovery success depends on phase, margin and awareness.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Loss of the protective barrier against an actual exceedance removes an assumed safety net and can lead toward loss of control or structural exceedance; classified Hazardous given crew can still recover manually within the envelope in most phases. Confirm whether unrecoverable near-ground exceedances drive this to Catastrophic. Note: the failure condition list for SF-003 named this M2 condition — it appears as a distinct malfunction not represented in the FCIM, flag for the engineer. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of envelope protection without degraded-law annunciation (crew unaware protection is absent)
fha.effAc: Protection is absent while the aircraft is flown as if it were present; an exceedance would proceed without intervention and without the annunciation that would have prompted crew caution.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties believing protection is available and take no compensating action, so any subsequent exceedance is met by neither the system nor a forewarned crew.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Unannunciated loss of protection removes the barrier and the crew cue simultaneously (the SDD states degraded laws are normally annunciated), so the crew fly with a false assumption of protection — more adverse than the annunciated case. Classified Hazardous; confirm whether the combination with a near-ground exceedance drives Catastrophic. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced envelope protection function in a degraded control law (partial loss, annunciated)
fha.effAc: A subset of envelope protections is available; the aircraft retains some but not all protective barriers, with reduced margin against the unprotected exceedances.
fha.effCrew: Degraded law is annunciated; crew are aware, apply increased vigilance and manual protection of the unprotected axes, with increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the provided material: the SDD confirms degraded laws exist and are annunciated but does NOT enumerate which protections are retained or lost in each degraded law. Without knowing which barrier(s) are absent (stall vs overspeed vs load-factor vs bank), the reduction in safety margin cannot be sized and severity is left blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight-envelope protection
fha.effAc: Aircraft remains controllable through the primary control path but the automatic protection against stall, overspeed and excessive attitude/load is absent; a subsequent crew or upset excursion is no longer arrested by the system. Per the SDD, loss of protection normally coincides with reversion to a degraded control law.
fha.effCrew: Degraded law is annunciated; crew must manually observe and respect envelope limits without protection assistance, increasing workload and reducing margin against an inadvertent exceedance.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a single classification from the document alone. Whether complete loss of envelope protection is Hazardous or Catastrophic depends on the residual control law and workload after reversion, which the SDD annunciates but does not characterise quantitatively; the outcome hinges on crew ability to respect limits manually — needs handling-qualities / workload assessment. Leaving severity empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Thrust response erroneous relative to crew command
fha.effAc: Thrust delivered differs from that commanded on one or more engines; with four engines on a wide span (outboard moment arm 28 m, 0.35 semi-span) an erroneous response on an outboard engine can produce asymmetric thrust and a directional-control demand, the SDD's stated sizing case for directional control.
fha.effCrew: Crew perceives thrust/aircraft response inconsistent with lever position; must diagnose and manage the affected engine (fuel shut-off / fire handle) and counter any resulting asymmetry with rudder.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on the magnitude, symmetry and phase of the erroneous response, none of which are quantified in the SDD. An erroneous outboard response near V1 (directional-control sizing case) trends more severe than a small symmetric error in cruise; without the FADEC failure characterisation and controllability data the class cannot be derived. Empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust change with no command
fha.effAc: One or more engines change thrust with no corresponding lever command; if confined to a single outboard engine this induces an uncommanded asymmetry about the 28 m moment arm requiring rudder to hold heading, and disturbs the intended flight path/speed schedule.
fha.effCrew: Crew observes an unexpected thrust/speed change, must identify the affected engine and manage it manually (autothrottle disconnect, fuel shut-off / fire handle) while countering asymmetry.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This condition is not present in the current FCIM for SF-004 and no aircraft-level effect magnitude is grounded in the SDD; severity depends on thrust-change size, symmetry and phase (e.g. uncommanded change near V1 vs cruise), which the document does not quantify. Empty per abstention — confirm the condition should exist and supply the controllability basis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust asymmetry across the aircraft
fha.effAc: Thrust becomes asymmetric across the span without crew command; an outboard asymmetry acts through the 28 m moment arm (0.35 semi-span), which the SDD identifies as the directional-control sizing case, generating a yawing/rolling moment the crew must counter with rudder.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the asymmetry, apply and hold corrective rudder, and manage the offending engine; workload rises, and directional control is the governing concern at low speed / high thrust.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Not present in the current FCIM for SF-004. Severity turns on asymmetry magnitude (single outboard vs multiple) and phase against available rudder authority; the SDD names the directional-control sizing case but gives no controllability margin or asymmetry magnitude to derive a class. Empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow thrust drift below crew detection threshold
fha.effAc: Thrust on one or more engines drifts slowly and is not detected by the crew (Unaware case); the aircraft departs the intended speed/thrust schedule gradually, and a slow drift on one outboard engine produces a slowly developing asymmetry the crew does not initially counter.
fha.effCrew: By definition the crew is unaware and takes no corrective action; the condition persists until it grows large enough to cross a detection threshold or manifests through a secondary cue (speed/heading trend).
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on the drift rate, the eventual magnitude before any cue is reached, and the flight phase — none quantified in the SDD, and the FCIM entry only names the condition. A slowly accumulating undetected asymmetry can trend more severe than a detected step; cannot derive a class without the drift/detection-threshold data. Empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous thrust indication masking an actual thrust error
fha.effAc: Displayed thrust does not reflect actual thrust produced; the aircraft operates on a false thrust datum. With the error masked the crew set/trim thrust to erroneous indication, so an actual under- or over-thrust persists uncorrected, degrading performance margins (climb gradient, terrain/obstacle clearance) without annunciation.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the actual thrust error; continue normal duties and manage thrust to the false indication, taking no corrective action. Discovery, if any, is late and by secondary cue.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Crew-unaware erroneous thrust datum can drive the aircraft outside intended performance/energy state without annunciation; on the effects stated a significant reduction in safety margins with increased crew workload once discovered supports Hazardous (↔ Extremely Remote). Confirm against phase-specific performance analysis; take-off/climb likely drives the worst case. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of thrust generation, symmetric
fha.effAc: Reduced total thrust available symmetrically; degraded climb gradient and reduced performance margin against the sector profile. Directional control is unaffected (symmetric). Severity of the outcome depends on the amount of thrust lost relative to the required performance for the phase and terrain.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via engine indications; manage thrust and, if required, revise the flight profile/diversion. Increased workload proportional to the deficit.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: 'partial' spans a continuum and the aircraft effect (climb-gradient/terrain-clearance shortfall) depends on the fraction of thrust lost, the flight phase, and the 600–2,000 nm low-flight-level sector performance — none of which is bounded here. Requires performance/one-engine-inoperative-analogue analysis per phase to derive severity. Do not default to a benign class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of thrust from one side producing thrust asymmetry
fha.effAc: Asymmetric thrust generates a yawing/rolling moment; an outboard engine at the 28 m (0.35 semi-span) moment arm is the sizing case for directional control. Aircraft controllable with rudder authority provided the sizing case is met; excursion risk at low speed/high thrust (V1/take-off) if authority is marginal. Continue-to-suitable-aerodrome is designed for loss of any one engine at/after V1.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via engine indications and yaw; apply rudder and adjust thrust, execute engine-out procedure and divert. High workload at the critical phase.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-engine-out asymmetry at the outboard 28 m moment arm is the directional-control sizing case; near V1/take-off the demand on rudder authority and crew workload is high. On the effects stated (controllable but with large safety-margin reduction and high workload at the critical phase) Hazardous (↔ Extremely Remote) is the suggested class; confirm against the directional-control sizing and the take-off/low-speed case which drives the worst phase. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of thrust generation
fha.effAc: Total loss of propulsive thrust across all four engines; aircraft cannot sustain flight and forced descent follows. No powered means to maintain the flight path; outcome is loss of the aircraft absent a successful forced landing. The design dispatch case covers loss of ONE engine only; all-engine loss is beyond it.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware; attempt relight/energy management and forced landing. Extreme workload with no assured recovery.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of thrust from all engines removes the ability to sustain flight; the effects stated (forced descent, loss of aircraft absent a successful forced landing) drive Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1×10⁻⁹/fh). Confirm; the independence of the four engine thrust sources and shared resources (FUE cross-feed gallery, EPS, bleed) must be substantiated in the PSSA/CCA to support the objective. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent reverse-thrust deployment in flight
fha.effAc: Uncommanded in-flight deployment of an inboard reverser produces a large asymmetric drag/thrust moment and disrupted airflow over the wing, degrading control and performance; potentially unrecoverable depending on phase and airspeed. Deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement with a mechanical sleeve lock, so the condition presupposes defeat of those inhibits.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via yaw/roll and annunciation; attempt to counter and stow. High-to-extreme workload; recovery not assured at high speed.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Inadvertent in-flight reverser deployment on an inboard engine produces severe asymmetric moment and wing-flow disruption; on the effects stated (potentially unrecoverable loss of control depending on phase/speed) Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1×10⁻⁹/fh) is suggested. Confirm; the multiple in-flight inhibits (WOW + radio-altimeter agreement + mechanical sleeve lock) and their independence are the mitigation to be substantiated in the PSSA/CCA. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of reverse-thrust deceleration capability
fha.effAc: No reverse-thrust deceleration available on landing; ground deceleration relies on wheel braking (SF-006) and aerodynamic drag. Whether the residual deceleration means keep rollout within the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement is not stated in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply maximum wheel braking; increased workload managing rollout and stopping margin on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD does not state how much of the 1,800 m vs ~1,080 m rollout margin depends on reverse thrust, so the aircraft-level effect (overrun risk on a semi-prepared strip with reverse lost) cannot be derived. Needs landing-performance data quantifying reverse-thrust contribution to the stopping case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced reverse-thrust deceleration capability
fha.effAc: Degraded reverse-thrust deceleration on landing; stopping performance reduced but partial reverse and wheel braking (SF-006) remain. Effect on the 1,800 m stopping requirement not stated.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply additional wheel braking to preserve stopping margin; increased workload on rollout.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the aircraft effect turns on how much stopping-distance margin is lost with reverse degraded, which the SDD does not quantify. Needs landing-performance data for the degraded-reverse case against the 1,800 m requirement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust on ground
fha.effAc: Asymmetric reverse thrust between the two inboard reversers produces a yawing moment during the ground roll, tending to deviate the aircraft from the runway centreline on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew counter the yaw with nose-wheel steering (SF-007) and asymmetric braking (SF-006); increased directional-control workload during rollout.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the resulting yaw magnitude and whether crew directional control (steering/braking) contains it within the runway is not stated. The SDD gives no residual-yaw-authority figure for asymmetric reverse on the ground, so the departure/excursion outcome cannot be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to stow reverse thrust after ground deceleration
fha.effAc: Reverse thrust remains deployed after the deceleration phase; residual reverse thrust and ingestion/debris exposure on a semi-prepared surface persist into low-speed rollout/taxi. Whether it back-drives directional control depends on symmetry.
fha.effCrew: Crew retard thrust levers and manage the un-stowed reverser; increased workload; possible need to shut down affected engine.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD does not state the aircraft-level consequence of a reverser that fails to stow (residual thrust at low speed, debris/ingestion on semi-prepared surface, symmetry). Needs the effect on controllability/engine handling to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded partial reverser deployment below detection threshold
fha.effAc: A partial, undetected reverser deployment in flight would act against the in-flight deployment inhibits (weight-on-wheels + radio-altimeter agreement, mechanical sleeve lock). If it produced spoiling/drag or asymmetric thrust on one inboard engine below the crew's detection threshold, it would affect thrust symmetry and drag; magnitude not stated.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware by definition (below detection threshold); no crew action taken; degradation carried into flight.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD does not state the aerodynamic/thrust effect of a below-threshold partial reverser deployment in flight, and the in-flight inhibits (WOW + radalt + mechanical lock) make the achievable deployment state undefined. Needs the residual asymmetric-yaw/drag effect to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous wheel-braking response to crew command (aware)
fha.effAc: Braking output differs from commanded — asymmetric or excessive braking induces a yawing moment / directional-control demand on a semi-prepared strip with limited rollout margin (1,800 m requirement vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout); crew aware via braking response and directional deviation and counters with steering, differential braking and reverse thrust (inboard reversers).
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to detect the erroneous response and maintain directional control during a high-workload, time-critical ground phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects support a directional-control/runway-excursion consequence on a semi-prepared surface, but the SDD does not quantify the yaw authority available against an erroneous-braking case, nor the margin outcome once crew countermeasures are applied; classification between Major and Hazardous cannot be derived from the provided material — left empty for engineering judgement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Low-level asymmetric braking below crew detection threshold (unaware)
fha.effAc: Small asymmetric braking bias below the crew detection threshold produces a slow directional drift; crew take no corrective action attributable to braking and continue duties normally, so the drift is countered late through general directional tracking.
fha.effCrew: No action taken regarding the condition (unaware); normal crew directional tracking absorbs the drift.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — A below-threshold asymmetry is by definition small; whether the resulting drift is nuisance-level or reaches a runway-edge consequence on a narrow semi-prepared strip cannot be derived from the provided material, which gives no track/strip-width or drift-rate data — left empty rather than reaching for a benign class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded wheel braking within landing-distance margin
fha.effAc: Reduced braking capability but stopping performance remains within the available margin — degradation absorbed within the operating margin between the 1,800 m landing-distance requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout, supplemented by inboard reverse thrust; aircraft stops on the available surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware of degraded braking (annunciation / feel) and manage deceleration with available means within margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Degradation that stays within the stated operating margin (1,800 m requirement vs ~1,080 m rollout) yields a slight reduction in safety margin / small increase in crew workload without an unsafe outcome — supports Minor (↔ Probable, 1e-3/fh). PROPOSED for confirmation; margin figure is preliminary SDD data. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of wheel braking capability
fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot decelerate by wheel braking on the ground. On landing at a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against a predicted ~1,080 m rollout, loss of wheel braking removes the primary means to stay within available surface; reverse thrust (inboard engines only) and residual drag remain but the operating margin the design rests on is lost, risking overrun of the semi-prepared surface. On a rejected take-off, inability to stop within the accelerate-stop distance is a critical concern.
fha.effCrew: Crew becomes aware (SF-006 aware case) of loss of braking response; high workload managing directional control and reverse thrust, executing overrun/go-around decision.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers. Flight crew only exposed to consequences of overrun.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects support a high-end classification (overrun of a short semi-prepared surface during RTO/landing), but selecting Hazardous vs Catastrophic requires the accelerate-stop and overrun-outcome analysis not present in the provided inputs — the residual deceleration from reverse thrust plus the ~720 m margin must be quantified. Left empty pending that engineering analysis rather than reaching for a value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded braking not annunciated (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Braking capability is reduced but the degradation is not annunciated. Crew plans and executes deceleration assuming full braking; on the short semi-prepared strip the achieved deceleration is below expectation, eroding the operating margin without warning and increasing overrun risk at the point where recovery options are fewest.
fha.effCrew: Crew continues normal duties and takes no corrective action regarding the degradation (unaware case), applies normal/autobrake expecting full performance; discovers shortfall late in the rollout.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers. Flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is an unannunciated deceleration shortfall against a short-margin surface, which is more severe than an annunciated degradation because the crew cannot compensate. Classifying (Major vs Hazardous) requires the achievable-deceleration-vs-required analysis and the size of the undetected shortfall, neither of which is in the provided inputs; left empty rather than guessing.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous nose-wheel steering response to crew command
fha.effAc: Nose-wheel steering responds erroneously (wrong sense or magnitude) to the crew command, producing an unintended directional deviation. At take-off/rollout speeds on a semi-prepared strip this can drive the aircraft toward the runway edge; the aircraft has a 160 m span and six main bogies, and a departure from the prepared surface risks gear/flotation exceedance and loss of directional control.
fha.effCrew: Crew becomes aware (SF-007 aware case) of the erroneous response, must counter with rudder/differential braking and reassess; elevated workload during a speed regime with little time margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers. Flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Directional deviation on a short unpaved strip at speed can be significant, but severity depends on the available counter-authority (rudder is sized for the outboard-engine-out case) and the speed/deviation dynamics — not derivable from the provided function definition alone. Left empty pending directional-control analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Low-level uncommanded nose-wheel steering drift below detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: A low-level uncommanded steering drift below the crew detection threshold produces a slow directional bias during ground roll. Because it is below detection, the crew does not counter it; on a narrow semi-prepared strip a slow accumulated lateral drift could carry the aircraft toward the surface edge over the roll distance.
fha.effCrew: Crew continues normal duties and takes no corrective action (unaware case), as the drift is below the detection threshold; may perceive only a need for small persistent corrections attributed to surface/wind.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers. Flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on how much lateral displacement a sub-detection-threshold drift accumulates over the take-off/landing roll relative to available surface width — neither the drift rate nor the strip width is given in the provided inputs. Cannot be derived from the function definition; left empty rather than assuming a benign outcome.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced nose-wheel steering authority
fha.effAc: Ground directional control degraded; larger steering inputs and greater reliance on differential braking and rudder to hold centreline on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip; controllability retained within reduced margin.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via steering response and can compensate with rudder and differential braking; increased workload during ground manoeuvring and landing rollout.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is a degraded but retained ground-control capability with crew compensation available; the SDD gives no crossing-limit or runway-excursion threshold at which reduced authority becomes an off-strip departure on the semi-prepared surface, so the aircraft-level outcome (nuisance vs. excursion) cannot be bounded from the provided material. Severity left empty pending the steering-authority-vs-controllability case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose-wheel steering
fha.effAc: No nose-wheel directional control; directional control on the ground maintained only by rudder (reducing with speed) and differential braking; ability to track the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip centreline significantly reduced, with risk of directional excursion at low speed and during turns.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware immediately; must control direction with differential braking and rudder, high workload, and may be unable to complete tight ground manoeuvres.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD confirms differential braking and rudder remain as alternative ground-directional means but gives no controllability substantiation for holding the semi-prepared centreline with steering lost; whether the residual capability keeps the outcome to a Minor ground-handling event or permits a runway excursion cannot be determined from the provided material. Severity left empty pending the ground-directional controllability case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of gear downlock integrity (crew aware case not applicable — condition is by definition unannunciated)
fha.effAc: A gear leg not positively downlocked may collapse on touchdown or during rollout; loss of ground support at that leg, asymmetric ground reaction, structural damage and potential loss of controllability on the ground at high energy on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effCrew: By definition the crew have no indication and take no action; downlock believed secure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect points toward gear collapse and loss of ground support at touchdown, but classification depends on how many legs the aircraft can lose while retaining support on the six-bogie arrangement and on the structural consequence of collapse at landing energy on a semi-prepared strip — none of which is quantified in the provided material (gear count is explicitly preliminary). Severity left empty pending the gear-collapse consequence case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded ground load-absorption capability
fha.effAc: Reduced capacity to absorb landing and taxi loads and to spread footprint pressure to the level the semi-prepared surface requires; on such a surface this can reduce flotation margin, increase rut depth and structural loading, and degrade the braking/rollout basis on which the 1,800 m requirement rests.
fha.effCrew: Crew may have limited or no indication of degraded absorption; no direct in-flight compensation available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD makes flotation and the 1,080 m predicted rollout against the 1,800 m requirement the operating margin, but gives no threshold at which degraded load-absorption erodes that margin into a structural or excursion outcome, and gear/flotation sizing is explicitly preliminary. The aircraft-level effect cannot be bounded from the provided material. Severity left empty pending the flotation/load-absorption margin case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced flotation on semi-prepared surface (partial loss of ground support / load-absorption; degraded footprint pressure spreading)
fha.effAc: Footprint pressure exceeds what the semi-prepared surface can bear; gear sinkage / rutting increases rolling resistance and steering/braking effectiveness on the strip degrades; risk of a bogie digging in during rollout or taxi on the unpaved surface.
fha.effCrew: Increased directional-control and braking workload on the strip; crew may need to reduce speed / abort taxi.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the provided material. The SDD makes flotation on the 1,800 m semi-prepared surface the LDG sizing case but does not state the aircraft-level outcome of a PARTIAL flotation loss (e.g. whether degraded flotation causes only extended rollout within the ~1,080 m predicted vs. 1,800 m required margin, a bogie dig-in/excursion, or structural gear damage). Severity left empty pending the effect of reduced flotation on landing distance/controllability. Note this exact PL2 condition is not present as a distinct row in the SF-008 FCIM.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of flotation margin on semi-prepared surface (crew unaware; flotation margin degraded without annunciation)
fha.effAc: Flotation margin against the semi-prepared surface is eroded without crew awareness; the aircraft operates onto/along a strip its footprint can no longer safely bear, with sinkage, rutting or a bogie dig-in occurring without the crew having reduced speed or aborted; the operating margin between the 1,080 m predicted rollout and the 1,800 m requirement is consumed unknowingly.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties taking no mitigating action because the loss is not annunciated; first indication is degraded ground handling / excursion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the provided material. The SDD identifies flotation on the semi-prepared surface as the sizing rationale but does not state the aircraft-level consequence of an UNDETECTED flotation-margin loss (excursion, gear collapse, or merely extended rollout). Because the condition is unaware, severity would turn on that outcome, which the SDD does not give. Left empty pending effects definition.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground support and load-absorption (gear unable to support the aircraft or absorb landing/ground loads)
fha.effAc: The gear cannot support the aircraft or absorb the touchdown/landing loads; loss of the ground load path at or near touchdown implies gear collapse and uncontrolled contact of the airframe with the surface, with attendant structural damage and fuel-system/fire exposure in the collapse.
fha.effCrew: Flight crew subject to a collapse/ground-impact event with limited or no available recovery once support is lost.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than the flight crew, who are exposed to the collapse event.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for engineer confirmation. Derived from the stated effect: total loss of the ground support/load-absorption path at touchdown implies gear collapse and uncontrolled airframe contact with the surface, an outcome consistent with a Catastrophic failure condition (multiple fatalities / hull loss) under §25.1309 / AC 25.1309-1B. The SDD does not quantify the collapse outcome, so the class is a proposal, not established; confirm against the structural/landing-load analysis and the worst applicable phase. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Misleading flight information displayed (crew aware; erroneous flight/attitude/air-data presented on the primary displays with standby indication available)
fha.effAc: Erroneous primary flight information (attitude / air data) presented to the crew; if acted upon before detection, control inputs may drive the aircraft toward an unsafe state or envelope exceedance. The independent standby instrument shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries and provides an independent comparison, and dissimilar FCC voting bounds propagation.
fha.effCrew: Crew become aware via disagreement between primary displays and the independent standby instrument / cross-checks and revert to standby data; increased workload to detect the disagreement and identify the valid source.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for engineer confirmation. Derived from the stated aware effect: misleading primary flight information is detectable against the independent standby instrument (which shares no supply, sensor or processing) and cross-checks, so the crew reverts to valid data with increased workload; this supports Major (significant reduction in safety margins / workload) rather than Hazardous, provided the disagreement is reliably annunciated/detectable. Confirm the detectability assumption and the worst phase (approach/landing typically drives the class). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Misleading navigation information displayed (crew aware; erroneous position/navigation information presented)
fha.effAc: Erroneous navigation/position information presented; if acted upon it can lead to track/path error and, in the approach and low-flight-level IFR profile flown to a semi-prepared strip, reduced terrain/obstacle separation before the error is detected. Dual radio/satellite navigation, dual flight management and independent standby indication provide comparison sources for the crew to detect and cross-check.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the error via navigation-source comparison (dual FMS, dual nav) and cross-checks and revert to a valid source; increased workload to identify and isolate the faulty source, particularly during approach.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot firmly classify from the provided material. The SDD supports that navigation information is presented and that dual navigation / dual FMS provide comparison sources, but it does not state the aircraft-level worst-case outcome of misleading navigation in the low-flight-level IFR / semi-prepared-strip approach case (whether detectable comparison keeps this Major or whether an undetected phase drives it higher). Severity left empty pending an effects/detectability determination for the approach case; do not default to a benign class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight and navigation information display
fha.effAc: All primary display of flight and navigation information lost; aircraft controllable only on the independent standby attitude/airspeed/altitude instrument (AVI §5.11.2), with no primary navigation presentation.
fha.effCrew: Crew reverts to the independent standby instrument for basic control; greatly increased workload, no primary situational or navigational picture, degraded ability to navigate to and fly an approach at a semi-prepared strip in IMC.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold not occupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Standby instrument shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries (§5.11.3), so basic controlled flight remains available — bounds the outcome below Catastrophic; but loss of all primary flight and navigation display in low-level IFR imposes a large workload increase and materially reduces safety margins, consistent with Hazardous. Confirm against IMC/approach exposure. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of primary display with standby indication available
fha.effAc: Primary flight/navigation display lost but the independent standby attitude/airspeed/altitude indication remains available; aircraft remains controllable on standby.
fha.effCrew: Crew uses standby indication as annunciated; increased workload and reduced information, but basic control and situational reference retained.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold not occupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With standby indication explicitly available and independent of the primaries (§5.11.3), effect is a significant reduction in capability/increase in workload rather than a large one — consistent with Major. Confirm whether navigation reference is adequately retained via standby/other means. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of navigation information only
fha.effAc: Loss of navigation information presentation while flight (attitude/air-data) information remains displayed; aircraft controllable and on-attitude but without navigational guidance.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains full flight-information display for control; navigational task is degraded, requiring alternate/backup navigation means to continue to and land at the semi-prepared destination.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold not occupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD confirms navigation is provided (dual radio/satnav, dual FMC) but does not state the aircraft-level consequence of losing navigation alone, nor the available reversion (e.g. remaining nav sources, diversion capability) at the low-flight-level IFR concept. Cannot derive severity without the effect of navigation loss on completing the mission/diversion — engineer to supply.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected misleading navigation information
fha.effAc: Displayed navigation information is erroneous and not annunciated; aircraft may be flown off intended track/approach path with no cue, risking terrain/obstacle proximity, especially into a semi-prepared strip in IMC.
fha.effCrew: Crew, unaware, navigates on false position/guidance; detection depends on cross-check against independent navigation sources, which is not assured for an unannunciated failure.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold not occupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction is clear (undetected off-track navigation), but the aircraft-level outcome depends on available independent navigation cross-checks, terrain environment of the semi-prepared destination, and whether the standby/other sources catch the error — none of which the SDD states at aircraft level. Cannot derive severity without that; engineer to supply the navigation-integrity/cross-check basis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous or spurious crew alert presented (alerting function operating differently from intended)
fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft state; a false or erroneous alert can trigger an unnecessary crew procedure or reconfiguration of an otherwise healthy system.
fha.effCrew: Crew presented misleading status; may divert attention, execute an unwarranted procedure, or lose confidence in the alerting list, increasing workload and error likelihood.
fha.effPax: None carried in flight; hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on which spurious alert is presented and the crew action it induces (a spurious fire/engine alert vs a nuisance advisory drive very different outcomes) — the SDD describes a single consolidated prioritised list but does not bound the range of alerts or the induced crew action, so the aircraft-level effect cannot be classified without that scope. Effect range plausibly Minor→Hazardous; left empty pending engineering judgment on worst-case induced action.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Crew alert presented with incorrect priority (correct condition annunciated but mis-ranked in the list)
fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft state; a time-critical condition may be de-prioritised so the crew acts late or acts on a lower-priority item first.
fha.effCrew: Crew may address alerts in the wrong order, delaying response to the most urgent condition; increased decision workload and risk of mishandling a time-critical failure.
fha.effPax: None carried in flight; hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The consequence hinges on whether a time-critical (e.g. fire, engine, envelope) alert is the one mis-ranked and how much delay results; the SDD states the list is prioritised across every system but does not identify which conditions are time-critical or the delay tolerance, so no aircraft effect can be bounded. Cannot classify without the alert set and criticality timing.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected failure to annunciate a real condition (valid alert not presented, unannunciated)
fha.effAc: A real system condition proceeds without crew warning; the aircraft continues in a degraded/failed state with no crew corrective action, allowing the underlying failure to develop unchecked.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware of a genuine failure; no procedure initiated; loss of the primary means by which the crew learns what has failed.
fha.effPax: None carried in flight; hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unannunciated (latent) loss of alerting for a real condition is bounded by the worst underlying condition it masks; the SDD confirms alerting consolidates every system's status but does not enumerate which conditions rely solely on this alerting path for detection, so the worst masked condition — and hence severity — cannot be established. Left empty pending the set of conditions whose sole warning is this function; plausibly up to Hazardous if a time-critical condition is masked.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of crew alerting coverage (some conditions no longer annunciated; remainder of alerting available)
fha.effAc: Aircraft state unaffected directly; failures in the un-covered subset proceed without warning while the rest of the alerting list continues to function.
fha.effCrew: Reduced coverage: crew warned of some conditions but not others; if the loss is annunciated, crew may apply increased vigilance; if not, crew operate unaware of the gap.
fha.effPax: None carried in flight; hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on which subset of conditions loses coverage and whether the coverage loss itself is annunciated (the SDD notes dual independent alerting channels but does not define the partial-coverage failure set or its annunciation), so the aircraft-level effect cannot be bounded. Cannot classify without the affected condition subset and its detection status.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of alert prioritisation (all conditions still annunciated, but presented without prioritised ranking)
