fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft state; with multiple concurrent alerts the crew has no ranking to identify the most urgent condition first, risking late action on a time-critical failure.
fha.effCrew: During multi-failure events the crew must triage an unranked list, increasing decision workload and the risk of addressing a low-priority item before a time-critical one.
fha.effPax: None carried in flight; hold unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Consequence is driven by the multi-alert case and how much crew delay/error an unranked list induces on a time-critical condition; the SDD confirms prioritisation is a defined feature of the list but does not quantify concurrent-alert scenarios or the workload/severity coupling (AC 25.1309 workload↔severity ladder needs engineering judgment). Cannot classify without that data. NOTE: no existing SF-010 FCIM condition matches PL2 — confirm before this row is retained.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected suppression of a valid crew alert (alerting present but silently drops/suppresses a real condition)
fha.effAc: A genuine system condition occurs but the consolidating alert is silently suppressed; the aircraft state degrades with no annunciation, so any protective crew action tied to that alert is not triggered until the condition is discovered by other means.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware of the underlying condition; loss of the intended time-critical prompt increases workload and delays or omits the required procedure. Worst-case effect depends on which alert is suppressed.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no direct occupant effect (crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the aircraft-function definition alone: severity of an UNDETECTED suppressed alert is set by WHICH underlying condition goes unannounced (e.g. fire vs a minor status), which the alerting function definition does not bound. Engineer to classify against the worst credible suppressed alert, or split by alert criticality.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of consolidated crew alerting
fha.effAc: No consolidated prioritised alert list or associated procedures presented; the single means of telling the crew what has failed and what to do is lost. Subsequent system failures are not annunciated through the alerting channel, so protective and reconfiguration actions are not prompted.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in crew workload: the crew must detect, prioritise and diagnose failures from raw display data without the consolidated list or its procedures, degrading situational awareness across all subsequent events.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no direct occupant effect (crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Complete loss of the alerting/procedure consolidation is a significant reduction in safety margin and a significant increase in crew workload — a Major indicator per the §25.1309 ladder. Underlying system indications remain on the displays, and alerting is driven by two independent channels (so total loss is not the design-basis single failure), which argues against Hazardous; confirm against the worst combined case where a subsequent failure goes unprompted. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous standby attitude / airspeed / altitude display (misleading standby indication, crew aware via disagreement with primaries)
fha.effAc: The independent standby instrument displays erroneous attitude/airspeed/altitude. With the primary displays available and valid, the standby disagrees with them; the crew has a majority reference and the standby is the outlier to be rejected.
fha.effCrew: Crew become aware through disagreement between the standby and the primary displays and standby engine/nav data; they reject the standby and fly the primaries. Increased workload and a period of ambiguity while the disagreeing source is identified.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no direct occupant effect (crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. With valid primaries as the cross-check, an erroneous but detected standby is a discrepancy the crew resolves against the majority — a reduction in safety margin / increase in workload consistent with Major rather than Hazardous. Depends on the assumption the primaries remain valid and available when the standby errs (SDD states standby shares no supply/sensor/processing with primaries). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected misleading standby indication agreeing with a faulted primary (both the primary source and the independent standby show the same erroneous attitude/airspeed/altitude)
fha.effAc: The standby, whose purpose is to be the independent cross-check, presents misleading data that agrees with a faulted primary. The one independent reference intended to break a common erroneous display is defeated, so the crew has no valid source to detect that the presented flight information is wrong; potential for loss of control if erroneous attitude/airspeed is flown.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue to fly on flight information they have no independent means to distinguish as false; no disagreement is annunciated. Recovery depends on other cues that may be absent — worst case, control of the aircraft is lost.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no direct occupant effect (crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Undetected misleading primary flight information with the independent standby corroborating the error removes the last cross-check the design relies on; flying erroneous attitude/airspeed with no means of detection can result in loss of the aircraft — the Catastrophic indicator. The classification hinges on the standby's independence claim (shares no supply/sensor/processing) meaning simultaneous agreeing error is not a common-cause single event; confirm this is truly a residual, not a design-basis, condition. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one standby attitude / airspeed / altitude parameter (partial loss of independent standby indication)
fha.effAc: One standby parameter (attitude, airspeed or altitude) is lost while the primary displays remain available. The independent backup reference is degraded but the primaries continue to provide that parameter.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain full flight information from the primary displays; the loss is annunciated and reduces the independent standby cross-check available for the affected parameter. Minor increase in workload / reduction in backup margin, with no immediate operational consequence.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no direct occupant effect (crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. With the primary displays intact, loss of a single standby parameter is a slight reduction in safety margin (backup depth) — a Minor indicator. Assumes the primaries provide the affected parameter and remain available; if the loss is coincident with a primary-display failure the classification would be more severe (that combination belongs in the PSSA, not this single-condition row). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of independent standby indication
fha.effAc: Loss of the independent attitude/airspeed/altitude source that shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays; aircraft remains controllable on the primary display chain but the dissimilar back-up against a common-mode display failure is gone.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain primary flight and navigation displays; no immediate control effect, but the independent means of detecting/riding through a total or misleading primary-display failure is unavailable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: SDD: the standby instrument 'shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays'. Loss of the back-up alone, with primary displays available, is a significant reduction in safety margin (a latent second failure now reaches misleading/total-loss display) — proposed Major; confirm against the primary-display architecture and whether standby is dispatch-critical. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pressurisation control / uncommanded differential change
fha.effAc: Outflow-valve/controller commands an incorrect differential; structure protected by independent positive and negative relief valves, but an erroneous control transient can drive cabin altitude or differential away from schedule up to the relief thresholds.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted via cabin altitude / differential indication; assumed to select manual pressurisation mode or the pneumatic backup and, if cabin altitude excursion occurs, don oxygen and descend.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the hold pressurisation differential is preliminary ('approximately 8,800 m hold altitude equivalent', not frozen) and the SDD gives no rate-of-change, decompression-time or cabin-altitude excursion the erroneous control can reach before relief/crew action. Severity depends on the achievable cabin-altitude excursion vs crew oxygen availability — provide the frozen differential and control-authority limits.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected slow drift of cabin differential outside limits
fha.effAc: Cabin differential drifts outside limits without annunciation; independent positive/negative relief protects the structure, but the drift is not detected by the crew until relief operates or a symptom appears.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and continue normal duties, taking no action; a slow cabin-altitude climb could progress toward hypoxia onset before any symptom prompts action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the undetected/unaware case turns on the cabin-altitude the drift can reach and the time to hypoxia relative to the low-pressure/cabin-altitude alerting, none of which the SDD quantifies, and the hold differential is preliminary. Provide the alerting thresholds and the drift-to-hypoxia time to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of flight deck conditioning only
fha.effAc: Flight deck conditioning lost while pressurisation control and hold conditioning are unaffected; SDD permits single-pack operation and the flight deck is a separate conditioning zone from the hold.
fha.effCrew: Flight-deck thermal/air-quality environment degrades over time, increasing crew discomfort and workload; no immediate loss of pressurisation or control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the SDD confirms the flight deck is a separate conditioning zone and single-pack operation is permitted, but gives no crew-environment tolerance data (temperature/CO2 rise vs time) to judge whether the effect is a slight or significant increase in crew workload. Provide the conditioning-loss environmental envelope to classify (candidate Minor pending that data).. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of hold conditioning only (single-pack degraded schedule)
fha.effAc: Reduced hold conditioning schedule on single-pack operation; pressurisation control of the flight deck and structural relief retained. Hold is unoccupied in flight and carries a single blade with no crew or passenger exposure to hold environment.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains flight-deck conditioning and pressurisation; annunciated pack configuration; no immediate handling or workload impact stated in the description.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-pack operation is expressly permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule, and the hold is unoccupied; flight-deck conditioning and pressurisation control are retained, so the effect is a slight reduction in capability with no direct crew/occupant hazard. Engineer to confirm against structural/cargo temperature limits not stated here. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight deck and hold pressurisation control
fha.effAc: Loss of active pressurisation control of both flight deck and hold; independent positive/negative mechanical relief still protects the structure. Loss of controlled cabin altitude at up to FL260 maximum operating altitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew loses controlled flight-deck cabin altitude and must manage a depressurisation event, don crew oxygen and descend/divert; the resulting cabin-altitude exposure and required workload at FL260 are not quantified in the description.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the description states a maximum operating altitude of FL260 and provides crew oxygen for depressurisation and diversion, but does not state the resulting cabin-altitude exposure, time of useful consciousness, or diversion time on which the crew/occupant effect and hence severity depend. Provide the FL260 depressurisation profile and oxygen diversion-time basis to derive the class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous lock indication (locked shown, not locked)
fha.effAc: Nose visor forms part of the pressure boundary and the forward fuselage structural load path when closed; a false 'locked' indication with the door not fully locked risks loss of pressure boundary and structural load path in flight, up to loss of the door. Dual dissimilar sensing normally provides an independent second path, but a single erroneous path corrupts the presented lock status.
fha.effCrew: Crew and take-off configuration monitor are misled into believing the door is locked; the second dissimilar sensing path (mechanical visual indicator) remains available to catch the disagreement before or during dispatch.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: The door is a single-load-path pressure boundary and structural element; a misleading 'locked' indication defeats the take-off configuration check and could permit dispatch with the door not locked, but dual dissimilar independently-routed sensing gives an independent means to detect the disagreement. Proposed Hazardous pending confirmation of whether both crew-visible paths must agree before dispatch. Engineer to confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded unlock / latch release with no crew command
fha.effAc: Uncommanded release of the eight locking pins and/or twelve latches in flight would open the nose pressure boundary and remove the forward fuselage structural load path, up to in-flight loss of the door. A pressure interlock requires residual differential below 0.1 psi before the lock actuator will run, and the pins prevent latch back-drive, so an in-flight release requires defeat of those interlocks.
fha.effCrew: Sudden depressurisation and structural event with no prior crew command; crew must respond to an unannunciated door-open condition in flight.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded in-flight opening of a single-load-path pressure boundary and structural element is a potential loss of the aircraft; the pressure interlock and separate pin actuator reduce likelihood but the effect if it occurs supports the most severe class. Proposed Catastrophic pending confirmation of the effect of in-flight door loss on controllability. Engineer to confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous lock indication with both sensing paths misreading
fha.effAc: Both dissimilar sensing paths (proximity harness and mechanical indicator) misread, so the not-locked state of the single-load-path pressure boundary and structural element is undetected by crew and by the take-off configuration monitor, removing every indicated means to catch the condition before or during flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no indication that the door is not locked; they continue normal duties and take no protective action, so no crew mitigation is available for a subsequent loss of pressure boundary or structural load path.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With both independent sensing paths failed the not-locked condition is undetected, defeating the dispatch check and leaving no crew mitigation for a potential in-flight loss of the pressure boundary and structural load path; the effect on a single-load-path door supports the most severe class. Proposed Catastrophic pending confirmation of the door-loss controllability effect. Engineer to confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one lock sensing/indication path for the nose pressure boundary (crew aware — remaining dissimilar path still indicates lock status)
fha.effAc: Nose door lock status remains determinable via the second, dissimilar and independently routed sensing path; pressure boundary and structural closure integrity unaffected by the sensing loss alone.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain valid lock indication from the surviving path and via the take-off configuration monitor; degraded monitoring redundancy annunciated; dispatch decision required.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effect is loss of one of two dissimilar independent lock-sensing paths with the pressure/structural function intact and the second path still indicating; a slight reduction in safety margin / monitoring redundancy → proposed Minor. Confirm against §25.783/pressure-boundary special condition once the door SC is defined. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose pressure boundary closure/lock — door not closed and locked, or unlocks/opens when it should remain secured
fha.effAc: Loss of the forward pressure boundary and of a primary forward-fuselage structural load path; potential in-flight loss of the nose visor with consequent rapid depressurisation and structural failure of the forward fuselage.
fha.effCrew: Sudden depressurisation and potential loss of structural integrity; crew oxygen required; controllability may be compromised depending on the departing structure; excessive workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: The SDD treats the closed nose visor as both the pressure boundary and a primary forward-fuselage structural load path with no structural redundancy; total loss in flight implies loss of pressure boundary plus loss of a single structural load path → proposed Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh). Confirm against the anticipated nose-door structural/pressure special condition. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous anti-ice operation / undetected loss of airframe surface and engine-inlet anti-ice protection in icing (crew aware — degraded-zone annunciation available)
fha.effAc: Ice accretion on a wing leading edge or engine inlet cowl where protection is expected, or erroneous/spurious anti-ice operation; degraded aerodynamic performance and/or engine inlet ice risk in the icing envelope.
fha.effCrew: Loss of an anti-ice zone is annunciated; crew assumed to exit icing, select manual protection where available and apply the icing performance penalty; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD establishes anti-ice coverage and that a lost electrical zone is annunciated, but does not state the aircraft-level performance/handling or engine-inlet consequence of ice accretion on a specific surface/inlet in the certification icing envelope; the aircraft effect that would drive severity is not grounded in the provided functions — need the icing-envelope handling/performance and inlet-ice substantiation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded anti-ice bleed demand reducing environmental pack capacity
fha.effAc: An uncommanded anti-ice bleed demand imposes a bleed load that reduces available pack capacity; the SDD does not state the resulting aircraft-level pressurisation/conditioning consequence.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD notes IPS presents 'a bleed demand to the environmental system that reduces pack capacity when in use', but the aircraft-level consequence of an UNCOMMANDED demand — degree of pack-capacity reduction, whether single-pack conditioning limits are breached, and the resulting cabin/hold conditioning effect — is not stated; cannot derive a severity without the pressurisation/conditioning effect. Missing: quantified pack-capacity margin and ECS single-pack schedule.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ice protection: loss of anti-ice on one zone / one protected surface
fha.effAc: Ice may accrete on one protected surface or inlet zone in icing conditions; remaining zones protected. Aerodynamic/inlet effect confined to the affected surface; degree of degradation not established from the definition.
fha.effCrew: Lost zone is annunciated (electrical zones annunciated per IPS); crew can select manual operation and may exit/avoid icing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the SDD does not state the icing envelope of the cert basis nor which single surface/inlet is flight-critical, so the aircraft-level consequence of losing one zone in icing is not derivable from the function definition. Needs icing exposure and per-surface criticality.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of wing or cowl bleed anti-ice protection on one side
fha.effAc: Bleed anti-ice to wing leading edges / engine inlet cowls lost on one side in icing conditions; opposite side still protected via cross-bleed manifold. Asymmetric ice accretion possible on wing/inlets of the affected side.
fha.effCrew: Bleed protection remains available from either side through the cross-bleed manifold; crew may cross-feed bleed. Degradation extent not established from the definition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the icing envelope and the handling/thrust consequence of asymmetric wing/inlet ice are not stated, so the aircraft-level effect (and whether asymmetry is controllable) is not derivable from the function definition. Needs icing exposure and asymmetric-ice handling assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of airframe surface and engine-inlet anti-ice protection
fha.effAc: No anti-ice on wing leading edges, engine inlet cowls or stabiliser surfaces. In icing conditions, unchecked ice accretion degrades lift/drag, control-surface effectiveness and engine-inlet integrity across all protected surfaces simultaneously; potential for significant performance loss and engine ingestion/damage.
fha.effCrew: Detection is advisory; crew must recognise loss and exit icing conditions. Workload and difficulty increased managing a diversion out of icing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED: complete simultaneous loss of all anti-ice, if encountered in the icing envelope, drives large multi-surface performance/handling and inlet degradation with reliance on crew recognising an advisory-only condition and exiting icing — consistent with Hazardous (Severe-Major). Leans on the assumption the aircraft is dispatched into / can encounter known icing; if the aircraft is never certified for icing the classification drops. Confirm icing exposure. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous heating control or undetected loss of a heated probe/port/windshield element
fha.effAc: A heated probe or static port may ice undetected, corrupting the air data (airspeed/altitude/AoA) derived from it; erroneous or misleading primary parameters possible if the affected sensor feeds a display path. Extent depends on which element and whether the primary/standby air data source is affected.
fha.effCrew: Undetected loss means the crew continue normally and may act on corrupted air data before recognising a discrepancy; standby instrument shares no sensor with the primaries and may provide a comparison.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the definition does not identify which probe/port drives a flight-critical air-data path, nor the exposure to icing, so whether undetected corruption reaches misleading primary information (potentially Hazardous) or is caught by comparison is not derivable. Needs air-data source criticality and icing exposure.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of windshield heating
fha.effAc: Windshield may fog or ice in icing/precipitation conditions, degrading external visibility. No effect on flight-path control surfaces or air data.
fha.effCrew: Reduced forward visibility; crew workload increased particularly for the visual segment of approach/landing. Element is monitored individually so loss is detectable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the aircraft-level consequence of reduced windshield visibility depends on the operating concept (IFR to a semi-prepared strip) and the icing/precipitation exposure at the visual segment, neither of which is quantified in the definition. Needs visibility-dependence of the approach and icing exposure.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of probe/port heating corrupting air data below the monitor threshold
fha.effAc: Probe/port icing corrupts air data (airspeed/altitude/AoA) fed to the primary displays; corruption is below the individual-element monitor threshold so no annunciation is raised.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally, unaware; act on misleading air data, potentially flying erroneous speed/attitude in icing conditions.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond the aircraft outcome.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected misleading primary air data with the crew unaware is a loss-of-integrity condition. PROPOSED — could be Catastrophic; not grounded: how the three ADIRUs, standby instrument voting and any air-data comparator detect/reject a single corrupted probe below threshold. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of heating on one probe/port/windshield element
fha.effAc: One heated element loses protection; individual monitoring annunciates the lost element; remaining redundant probes/ports preserve air data.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to the lost element; assumed to reference the remaining sources / apply icing procedure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single annunciated element loss with remaining air-data sources available; effect bounded by monitoring and redundancy. PROPOSED — not grounded: the air-data source count and whether one element loss reduces a required independent channel below dispatch minima. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of a single windshield heating element
fha.effAc: One windshield panel loses anti-ice/anti-fog heating; potential local vision degradation through that panel; monitored per element.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted; assumed to use the remaining clear panel(s) for external vision.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of one windshield panel's heating degrades vision through that panel only, with other panels available. PROPOSED — not grounded: number of windshield panels and their per-crew-station assignment, needed to confirm remaining forward vision. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of probe, port and windshield heating
fha.effAc: All probes, static ports and windshields lose heating; in icing, air data across all channels becomes progressively unreliable and forward vision through all windshields degrades.
fha.effCrew: Multiple air-data and vision cues corrupt together; crew workload and ability to fly reliable references severely challenged in icing conditions.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond the aircraft outcome.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Simultaneous loss of air-data integrity on all channels plus forward vision in icing challenges continued safe flight. PROPOSED — not grounded: the common-cause path that would fail all heating together (single supply vs independent), which sets whether this condition is credible and its true severity. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous ice-detection advisory
fha.effAc: Ice detection presents an incorrect advisory (false positive or false negative); detection is advisory with manual ice-protection selection available at any time.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive a misleading advisory; may command anti-ice unnecessarily (performance penalty) or fail to select it when needed, though manual selection and other icing cues remain.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD states detection is advisory with manual selection always available, which caps the effect, but it is not grounded whether a false advisory drives any AUTOMATIC anti-ice activation or performance-penalty action, nor what other independent icing cues the crew have. Missing: automatic-activation logic and crew cross-check on a false advisory.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected failure to advise on actual ice accretion (detector fails to advise; no annunciation of the detection failure)
fha.effAc: Detection silently fails to advise while ice accretes; if the crew rely on the advisory for automatic activation, ice protection may not be commanded on and unprotected accretion degrades lift/drag, handling and stall margin. Manual selection remains available.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive neither an ice advisory nor a detection-fault indication; they continue normal duties and take no action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone. Aircraft-level severity depends on the credit taken for manual/other detection of icing and on the handling/performance penalty of unprotected accretion in the certified icing envelope — neither is stated. The unannunciated (latent) nature is captured; the effect magnitude is not derivable from the SDD.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded ice-accretion detection coverage (one ice detector lost or partial coverage)
fha.effAc: Two identical ice detectors are installed on opposite sides; loss of one leaves the other providing advisory coverage, and a lost element is annunciated. Detection capability reduced but not eliminated; manual selection remains available.
fha.effCrew: Crew are annunciated the degraded/lost element and retain the remaining detector plus manual selection.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone. With one of two detectors retained and the loss annunciated, effect is bounded, but the residual coverage adequacy and the credit for manual activation are not quantified in the SDD, so the aircraft-level outcome cannot be derived. Missing: whether single-detector coverage is sufficient for the certified icing envelope.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ice-accretion detection (both detectors lost; no automatic advisory)
fha.effAc: No automatic ice advisory available; automatic activation of ice protection is lost. The SDD states the system may be selected on manually at any time, so protection is retained if the crew select it; the aircraft-level effect turns on that manual reversion and on other icing cues.
fha.effCrew: Loss of detection is annunciated (lost elements are annunciated); crew must select ice protection manually and manage the icing environment.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone. The SDD provides manual selection at any time and annunciation of lost elements, so the outcome depends on the credit for manual reversion and other icing cues — not quantified. Missing: the certified reliance on automatic detection and the handling/performance consequence if manual protection is not selected in time.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous fire/overheat warning (false fire or overheat annunciation with no actual fire/overheat)
fha.effAc: A false fire/overheat warning may prompt an unwarranted engine/APU shutdown and fire-handle actuation (crew action, per SDD) or an unnecessary rejected take-off/diversion. Loss of a serviceable engine/APU reduces available thrust and system margins; on the ground with the APU unattended, automatic APU discharge and shutdown may occur without cause.
fha.effCrew: Crew workload and diversion decision-making increase; crew act on the warning per procedure (fire handle, shutdown), potentially shutting down a healthy engine and reconfiguring systems.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone. Aircraft-level severity depends on the credited crew procedure for a fire warning (confirmation before shutdown), the flight phase (e.g. asymmetric loss during take-off on four engines vs cruise), and whether spurious warnings are annunciated in a distinguishable way — none quantified in the SDD. Missing: crew confirmation credit and the propulsion/directional consequence of an unwarranted shutdown.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to warn on actual fire or overheat (crew aware detection is degraded/absent by other annunciation)
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: A real fire or overheat in a protected zone (engine nacelle, APU compartment, bleed duct run or main gear bay) progresses without a warning being raised; crew have some awareness that detection is unavailable and can apply precautionary procedures (e.g. reduce bleed, monitor, divert), but cannot confirm or localise an actual event.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware that detection/warning is impaired; assumed to apply precautionary measures and elect a diversion, with increased workload and reliance on secondary cues.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed directly.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects on the aircraft depend on which protected zone loses warning (an untended engine/APU fire versus a bleed-duct overheat differ materially) and on what precautionary crew action the impaired-but-aware state permits; the function definition and SDD do not fix a single worst-case zone or the residual protection assumed for the aware case, so a single severity cannot be grounded. Engineer to fix the governing zone and the credited aware-crew action.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected failure to warn on actual fire or overheat (crew unaware — no annunciation of the real event and no indication that detection has failed)
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: A real fire or overheat in a protected zone progresses with no warning and no crew awareness; no extinguishing or isolation is initiated. In an engine nacelle or APU compartment an undetected fire can propagate to adjacent structure, fuel and hydraulic services in the wing root/pylon, threatening continued safe flight. In the hold, which has smoke detection but no suppression, a missed warning removes the only line of defence.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action regarding the event; the omission is latent until the fire produces secondary effects.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed directly.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected, unannunciated fire in a nacelle/APU fire zone that is allowed to propagate to fuel and structure, with no crew action credited, plausibly prevents continued safe flight and landing — the worst-case outcome supports Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1×10^-9/fh). The SDD identifies these as fire zones with flammable fluid and high energy. Engineer to confirm against §25.1309. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded fire/overheat detection in a protected zone (reduced detection capability — e.g. one of two detection loops lost, reverting to single-loop logic)
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Detection in the affected zone continues at reduced integrity (single-loop rather than dual-loop AND logic), with an increased probability of a delayed or missed warning or of a spurious warning; the zone remains covered but with less margin.
fha.effCrew: Crew annunciated of the loss of one detection loop; assumed to monitor and treat the zone with heightened caution, applying dispatch/continuation judgement.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed directly.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of one detection loop degrades to the design's single-loop logic — the SDD states detection degrades to single-loop on loss of one loop — so coverage is retained with reduced redundancy and the aircraft's fire protection is not lost; a slight reduction in safety margin with a modest increase in crew workload is consistent with Minor (↔ Probable, 1×10^-3/fh). Engineer to confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of overheat detection on a monitored run (bleed duct run or main gear bay overheat detection lost)
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Overheat detection is lost on a bleed-duct run or in a main gear bay; a duct rupture/hot-air leak or a bay overheat (e.g. dragging brake) would progress without an overheat warning, allowing damage to adjacent structure and services before it is otherwise noticed. Fire-loop detection of the nacelle/APU zones is unaffected.
fha.effCrew: Crew annunciated of the loss of overheat detection on the affected run; assumed to apply bleed/brake precautionary procedures and rely on secondary indications (e.g. bleed pressure/temperature, brake temperature).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed directly.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of overheat detection on a bleed-duct run or gear bay removes early warning of a hot-air leak or bay overheat, permitting undetected damage until secondary effects appear — a significant reduction in safety margin with increased crew workload, consistent with Major (↔ Remote, 1×10^-5/fh), given the SDD fits overheat detection to the bleed duct runs and main gear bays. Engineer to confirm whether the worst-case bleed-duct case (proximity to fuel/structure at the wing root) warrants a higher class. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and overheat detection (no detection available in any protected zone)
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No fire or overheat warning is available anywhere — engine nacelles, APU compartment, bleed duct runs, main gear bays and hold. A fire in any fire zone (flammable fluid, high energy) would progress undetected, no extinguishing would be commanded, and propagation to fuel, hydraulics and primary structure could prevent continued safe flight and landing. In the unsuppressed hold, detection is the sole defence and is entirely absent.
fha.effCrew: Crew may be aware that all detection is lost (annunciated), but have no means to detect or localise an actual fire; assumed to divert to the nearest suitable aerodrome at elevated workload, without the ability to confirm or fight a fire until secondary effects manifest.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed directly.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of fire/overheat detection with the crew aware and able to elect an immediate diversion — but unable to detect an actual fire — is a large reduction in safety margin and physical crew distress; where the loss is annunciated and precautionary diversion is credited this is consistent with Hazardous (↔ Extremely Remote, 1×10^-7/fh). If total loss is combined with an actual undetected fire the outcome is worse; engineer to confirm the classification and whether the coincident-fire case is treated here or in the M3 condition. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent extinguisher discharge into a nacelle or APU compartment
fha.effAc: Loss of first-shot extinguishing agent for the affected engine pair or APU; if a subsequent real fire occurs in that zone the crew has depleted/absent agent. No immediate loss of any flight function. Nuisance agent discharge in the nacelle.
fha.effCrew: Fire discharge annunciation and possible spurious fire indication; crew workload to diagnose and manage; loss of an extinguishing shot for later use.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; not applicable to passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effect is depletion of one extinguishing shot with no immediate loss of a flight function; residual agent/redundancy (two bottles per engine pair, cross-plumbed) remains. Confirm against the fire-protection redundancy claim. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of engine/APU fire extinguishing to one nacelle or the APU
fha.effAc: No extinguishing capability into one nacelle of an engine pair or the APU compartment; a fire in that specific zone cannot be suppressed by fixed agent. Detection remains; other zones retain protection.
fha.effCrew: Fire in the affected zone would present but be un-extinguishable by fire handle; crew must manage by shutdown/isolation and diversion; loss of a safety barrier.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; not applicable to passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity of an unsuppressible fire in one zone depends on the consequence of an uncontained/sustained nacelle or APU fire in this configuration (structural, spread, control-run proximity), which the SDD describes topologically but does not classify. Requires particular-risk / fire-zone consequence input to derive.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of engine and APU fire extinguishing
fha.effAc: No fixed-agent extinguishing available to any engine nacelle or the APU; any fire in these fire zones cannot be suppressed. Detection remains functional. Loss of a fire-safety barrier aircraft-wide, latent until a fire occurs.
fha.effCrew: On any engine/APU fire the crew can shut down and isolate the affected engine/fuel but cannot extinguish; must divert with a possibly sustained fire; significant workload and no positive suppression means.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; not applicable to passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Classification requires the consequence of an unsuppressed sustained fire in a high-energy/flammable-fluid fire zone combined with the exposure of the latent loss until a fire occurs; the SDD provides zone/fire-zone topology but does not state the fire-consequence outcome. Provide fire-progression/particular-risk consequence to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous longitudinal restraint tension applied to the payload
fha.effAc: Restraint tension incorrect (over- or under-tensioned) relative to the required schedule; potential for inadequate longitudinal restraint of a single up-to-72.6 t blade, or induced load on the blade/hard points. Blade shift under longitudinal load cases would produce a large CG excursion.
fha.effCrew: In flight the crew has indication only and no in-flight adjustment; erroneous applied tension is set on the ground and carried into flight; crew reliant on tension monitoring and pre-flight checks.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; not applicable to passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive: the aircraft effect of erroneous applied tension depends on the blade structural/restraint limits and the CG-excursion consequence of a longitudinal shift, which the SDD flags as not yet frozen (restraint requirements 'were not written' for this payload). Provide the restraint load limits and CG-shift consequence to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of longitudinal payload restraint — the single unitised blade (up to 72.6 t, full hold length) is unrestrained longitudinally; lateral/vertical restraint by saddle geometry only
fha.effAc: Longitudinal migration of a 72.6 t unitised mass along the 108 m hold axis; large uncommanded CG shift and dynamic load into the hold floor hard points and airframe; potential loss of controllability and structural overload
fha.effCrew: Restraint condition annunciated (loss on two adjacent stations flagged as requiring immediate attention); crew cannot adjust restraint in flight (indication only)
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects support a severe/Catastrophic outcome for an uncontrolled CG shift of a 72.6 t mass, but the SDD does not quantify the migration distance, dynamic loads, or resulting CG excursion versus controllable/structural limits, and load paths are sized only such that loss of ONE strap is carried by neighbours — total loss is outside that stated case. Severity left empty pending the loading/structural and controllability case; not classifiable from the function definition alone.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded longitudinal restraint at one station — loss of restraint at a single saddle station with load carried by neighbouring stations
fha.effAc: Loss of one strap/station is carried by its neighbours per the stated load-path sizing; restraint maintained overall with reduced margin
fha.effCrew: Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight; crew has indication only, no in-flight adjustment
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD states loss of any one strap is carried by neighbours, implying restraint is maintained, but does not quantify the residual margin or the aircraft-level consequence of the degraded state, so the effect on the aircraft cannot be graded. Severity left empty pending the margin substantiation; do not assume benign.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Over-tension of a restraint strap — erroneous restraint tension applied above the intended value at a saddle station
fha.effAc: Excess tension imparts load into the blade profile at the conforming saddle interface and into the hold floor hard points; potential local overload of blade or hard point
fha.effCrew: Tension monitoring loop instruments every strap; erroneous/over-tension state assessed against annunciation coverage; no in-flight adjustment
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD notes narrow flex limits on the blade and no redundancy in the hold floor hard points, so over-tension could damage payload or structure, but the tension limits, blade allowables, and hard-point margins are not stated, and loading is a ground operation — the aircraft-level flight effect is not derivable from the function definition. Severity left empty pending tension/allowable data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous restraint-tension indication — the tension monitoring loop presents tension that does not reflect the actual strap tension
fha.effAc: No direct aircraft effect from indication alone; masks or falsely presents restraint state such that an actual degraded/loss condition (SF-019) may go unmanaged, or a valid loading is rejected on the ground
fha.effCrew: Crew has in-flight indication only; erroneous indication misleads the restraint-condition assessment and may drive an unwarranted diversion or fail to prompt attention where warranted
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The monitoring loop is a single instrumented loop (its coverage is a recorded item), so an erroneous indication that masks a real restraint loss inherits the (unquantified) SF-019 consequence, while a spurious indication is at most a nuisance/diversion. The aircraft effect depends on the SF-019 severity, which is itself unclassified this turn. Severity left empty pending SF-019 classification and monitoring-coverage substantiation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to annunciate an actual loss of tension — an actual strap/station tension loss occurs but is not annunciated to the crew
fha.effAc: An actual restraint degradation or loss (SF-019 class) is present but unmanaged; combined condition can progress toward CG shift / load-path overload of the 72.6 t unitised payload without crew awareness
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware; the annunciation that would flag a loss (any strap) or a two-adjacent-station restraint condition is not presented, so no assessment or diversion is initiated
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unannunciated, an actual tension loss deprives the crew of the only in-flight means of awareness (indication only, no adjustment), so this inherits the SF-019 degradation/loss consequence with no mitigating crew action — plausibly severe. But it is bounded by the underlying SF-019 severity, which is unquantified this turn (migration/CG/load magnitudes not stated), and depends on the single monitoring loop's undeclared coverage/latency. Severity left empty pending SF-019 classification and coverage substantiation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected failure to annunciate an actual loss of restraint-tension at one or more stations (monitor fails to alert on a real tension loss)
fha.effAc: An actual loss of strap tension progresses unannunciated; the crew receives no restraint alert and takes no action. Blade restraint is degraded without crew knowledge. Per the design the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours, so restraint is not immediately lost, but a progressing or multi-strap loss could reach the two-adjacent-station restraint condition undetected.
fha.effCrew: No indication; crew continue duties normally and take no restraint action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity turns on whether an undetected restraint degradation can progress to loss of blade restraint sufficient to threaten controlled flight, and on the coincident probability of an actual tension loss occurring while monitoring is failed. The provided function definition establishes the monitoring role and the neighbour-carry load path but does not state the aircraft-level consequence of an undetected multi-strap loss (CG shift / structural / control effect of a shifted 72.6 t blade). Effect on the aircraft is not established from the function definition alone — left empty pending the CRG restraint-loss consequence analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of restraint-tension monitoring at some stations (partial loss of monitoring coverage; other stations still monitored)
fha.effAc: Monitoring coverage is reduced but not lost; strap tension itself is unaffected. Restraint of the blade is unchanged; the crew retains tension indication over the remaining instrumented stations. Aware condition — loss of a monitoring channel is annunciated.
fha.effCrew: Crew are alerted to reduced monitoring coverage and can weigh dispatch/continuation against the retained coverage.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Minor: partial loss of a monitoring/indication function, annunciated, with no loss of the underlying restraint and with residual monitoring coverage over other stations. Effect is a modest reduction in crew awareness margin, not a loss of a required capability. Engineer to confirm against the coverage the design credits. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of restraint-tension monitoring (no strap tension indication available to the crew for any station)
fha.effAc: Strap tension is unaffected; the blade remains restrained by the winched-and-locked straps and saddle geometry. The crew loses all in-flight tension indication and therefore all in-flight awareness of any subsequent restraint degradation. There is no in-flight adjustment of restraint regardless.
fha.effCrew: Crew are alerted to loss of the monitoring loop; they continue with no in-flight visibility of strap tension and no means to detect a subsequent tension loss.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Loss of monitoring alone does not lose restraint, so the direct effect is loss of crew awareness. Severity depends on how much the safety case relies on in-flight tension monitoring to detect a developing restraint loss before it becomes hazardous (the tension loop is a single instrumented loop and its coverage is a recorded item). The function definition does not state the consequence of an undetected restraint loss, so the aircraft-level effect cannot be classified from it — left empty pending the CRG restraint-loss consequence analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous oxygen delivery pressure at the mask (crew breathing oxygen delivered at incorrect pressure)
fha.effAc: During a depressurisation, smoke/fume event, or the descent and diversion that follow, the flight crew rely on the mask supply. Erroneous delivery pressure degrades or prevents adequate crew oxygenation at altitude at the moment the supply is needed, impairing crew performance during the diversion.
fha.effCrew: Crew oxygenation compromised when the masks are required; potential impairment/incapacitation risk depending on the pressure error and cabin altitude at the maximum operating altitude (FL260).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers. No passenger oxygen is fitted.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Hazardous: erroneous mask delivery pressure impairs flight-crew oxygenation precisely when the crew depend on it (depressurisation / smoke event / diversion), producing a large reduction in crew capability at altitude. Classification assumes the condition is not simultaneous with loss of pressurisation across the whole crew such that all pilots are impaired at once (which would drive Catastrophic). Engineer to confirm against the crew-incapacitation scenario and coincident-failure assumptions. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew breathing oxygen supply
fha.effAc: No direct effect on the aircraft; the airframe continues to fly. Effect is on crew capability to manage a decompression/smoke event.
fha.effCrew: No breathing oxygen available to any crew station. In a concurrent loss-of-pressurisation or smoke/fume event at up to FL260 the crew have no protection for the emergency descent and diversion the system exists to cover; crew incapacitation is credible.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on the concurrency and probability of a decompression/smoke event coincident with total oxygen loss and on the cabin altitude actually reached at FL260 - not derivable from the OXY description alone. Left empty: the driving-case combination (INV concurrency with ECS decompression) must be established before classifying; do not reach for Catastrophic or a benign class without it.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced oxygen supply duration or reserve
fha.effAc: No direct effect on the aircraft.
fha.effCrew: Oxygen available but with reduced duration/reserve below the sized diversion time. Crew protection may run short before completion of descent and diversion from the maximum operating altitude.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify without the sized diversion duration, the actual reserve remaining under this condition, and the time to descend to a safe altitude from FL260 - none of these are quantified in the SDD. Severity turns on whether reduced reserve still covers the required diversion.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of oxygen to one or more mask stations
fha.effAc: No direct effect on the aircraft.
fha.effCrew: One or more mask stations without oxygen while others remain supplied. With a nominal complement of two and regulators independent per mask, loss at an occupied station removes protection for that crew member during a decompression/smoke event; the remaining crew member(s) retain protection.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Classification depends on how many stations are lost, whether an occupied station is affected, and whether single-pilot management of an emergency descent is credited - not resolvable from the SDD, which states regulators are independent per mask but does not bound the number of stations lost by a single cause.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow oxygen leak below the low-pressure alerting threshold
fha.effAc: No direct effect on the aircraft.
fha.effCrew: An undetected slow leak depletes cylinder contents below what indication/alerting reveals. Crew are unaware and take no action; on a subsequent decompression/smoke event the available oxygen may be less than the sized diversion reserve, discovered only on donning.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware condition: severity depends on the alerting threshold, the depletion reachable below it, and the residual reserve versus required diversion time - none quantified. The undetected nature routinely worsens the class relative to the aware PL, but the aircraft effect cannot be bounded from the SDD.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected off-specification oxygen delivered at the mask
fha.effAc: No direct effect on the aircraft.
fha.effCrew: Oxygen of incorrect concentration/pressure delivered at the mask without detection. During a decompression/smoke event the crew don masks believing them serviceable but receive off-specification gas; degraded crew performance or incapacitation is credible with no cue to prompt corrective action.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD does not characterise the delivery-quality failure (degree of off-specification, physiological effect at FL260 cabin altitudes) nor any downstream detection. The undetected misleading-delivery character is potentially serious but the aircraft/crew effect is not bounded by the provided material.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of crew breathing oxygen supply, undetected until the crew attempt to don masks
fha.effPax: N/A — hold is not occupied in flight; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded from the provided function definition. The SDD states the system supplies oxygen for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events and the ensuing descent/diversion, and that discovery is at donning, but it does not state the aircraft-level consequence of crew hypoxia/smoke exposure without oxygen. Needs: time-of-useful-consciousness at the operative cabin altitude, the flight phase(s) in which this condition manifests, the low-pressure alerting design credit, and whether crew incapacitation is credible before descent — none provided. Classify once the effect on the crew (and thence the aircraft) is stated.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected misleading flight information
fha.effAc: Displayed flight information (attitude/air-data) is erroneous and not annunciated; crew may act on false data, potentially commanding the aircraft outside a safe flight path with no cue to distrust the display.
fha.effCrew: Crew, unaware, continues normal duties acting on misleading primary data; only cross-check against the independent standby instrument (§5.11.3) provides a means to detect and recover, and detection is not assured.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold not occupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected misleading flight information acted upon in IMC can drive loss of control before the crew detects the disagreement; the independent standby exists but detection via cross-check is not guaranteed for an unannunciated failure, so the potential outcome is Catastrophic. Confirm detection/annunciation and standby cross-check credit. — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: The four systems FUE, HYD, EPS and EWS are resources, not aircraft functions, and are therefore excluded from the aircraft function list.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD classifies these as resources but the request is to author aircraft-level FUNCTIONS; I excluded them per the function-vs-resource modelling rule rather than authoring 'provide power' functions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the programme wants fuel storage/distribution or power availability captured as functions, additional top-level functions and their FHA rows would be added.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS from all add_function actions

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft themselves

assumptions.text: The nose-door structural load path and the hold floor hard points are structure, substantiated by structural/particular-risk analysis, not functional-FHA items; only the door lock/close/monitor behaviour is authored as a function.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly treats the door as a single load path and 'structure'; I split the behaviour (lock/monitor) from the structure per the function-vs-structure rule.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the engineer wants the door as a whole treated functionally, the sub-function boundary and its FHA/PRA linkage would change.
assumptions.usedFor: Sub-function 'Close, lock and monitor the nose pressure boundary'

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure

assumptions.text: Flight-envelope protection is authored as a distinct sub-function of trajectory control rather than folded into primary surface control.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes protection as a computer-hosted behaviour separable from actuation; whether it fails independently of surface control is an engineering call the SDD does not settle.
assumptions.ifWrong: If protection cannot fail independently of primary control, it should be merged into the primary-control sub-function, reducing the decomposition by one.

citations.quote: envelope protection active in the normal control law. Degraded laws are annunciated

assumptions.text: Reverse thrust is authored under 'Provide propulsive thrust' rather than under ground deceleration.
assumptions.rationale: Reverse is a propulsion behaviour but contributes to the 1,800 m ground-deceleration case; placement affects which top FHA it rolls into.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the programme prefers reverse under ground deceleration, the parent function of that sub-function changes and its FHA up-link moves.
assumptions.usedFor: Sub-function 'Provide reverse thrust for ground deceleration'

citations.quote: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only

assumptions.text: The crew-Aware vs Unaware split for SF-001 malfunctions relies on the FCS asymmetry/jam discretes alerting the crew, but the alert coverage for slow surface drift is not stated.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names asymmetry/jam discretes but does not state a detection threshold or whether slow drift is annunciated, so I could not ground the indication field for the Unaware row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If slow drift is in fact annunciated, the SF-001 Unaware row collapses and those malfunctions move to the Aware row only.

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes; high-lift position to the performance computation

assumptions.text: Thrust from one side producing asymmetry is treated as a partial-loss aircraft-level failure condition of SF-004 because directional control is the stated sizing case.
assumptions.rationale: The function list gives SF-004 at aircraft level only; I split symmetric vs asymmetric partial loss because the SDD identifies asymmetric thrust as the directional-control sizing case.
assumptions.ifWrong: If asymmetric thrust is handled entirely under SF-001 yaw authority, the SF-004 asymmetric partial-loss entry is redundant and should be removed.

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: Reverse thrust is available on ground only (in-flight deployment inhibited), so inadvertent in-flight deployment is a malfunction rather than a normal capability.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states in-flight deployment is inhibited; I relied on this to classify inadvertent in-flight deployment as a malfunction failure condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the inhibit is not credited, inadvertent in-flight deployment would need separate treatment and possibly its own function-level condition set.

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock

assumptions.text: Degraded wheel braking that stays within the landing-distance margin versus that which exceeds it are two distinct failure conditions.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives a rollout of ~1,080 m against an 1,800 m requirement and calls the margin the basis for assessing braking degradation, but does not enumerate the FCIM split.
assumptions.ifWrong: The two SF-006 partial-loss entries collapse to one and the downstream AFHA classification changes.

citations.quote: predicted landing rollout is approximately 1,080 m, and the margin between the two is the basis on which braking degradation is assessed

assumptions.text: Erroneous braking response and uncommanded/asymmetric braking are separately detectable and separately consequential, hence two malfunction entries.
assumptions.rationale: Control-axis malfunction pairing rule requires the split; the SDD confirms electrically signalled braking with per-wheel-pair anti-skid but does not list failure conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-006 malfunction cell merges to a single entry, hiding a failure condition.

citations.quote: electrically signalled, hydraulically actuated brake control

assumptions.text: An independent standby instrument survives a primary-display loss, so 'loss of primary with standby available' is a distinct partial-loss condition from complete loss of flight information.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the standby shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries, but the FCIM split is not written in the document.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-009 partial-loss entries and the SF-009/SF-010 combined condition change; the AFHA severity split changes.

citations.quote: an independent integrated standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.text: Some erroneous/misleading display and alerting behaviour can develop below crew detection thresholds, justifying a crew-Unaware row for SF-009 and SF-010.
assumptions.rationale: Detection means and thresholds are not defined in the SDD; erroneous data or a suppressed valid alert may present no cue.
assumptions.ifWrong: The Unaware rows for SF-009 and SF-010 are removed and the analysis treats these conditions as always crew-detected.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-009 Unaware row, SF-010 Unaware row

citations.quote: consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures

assumptions.text: Ground support / load absorption and flotation degradation on a semi-prepared surface are treated as functional-FHA conditions for SF-008 even though structural integrity itself is substantiated by structural analysis.
assumptions.rationale: SF-008 is authored as a function in the model; the SDD flags flotation and gear count as preliminary, so the degraded-flotation condition is retained but structural load-path integrity is out of FHA scope.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-008 flotation partial-loss entry moves to Particular Risk / structural substantiation rather than the FCIM.

citations.quote: Tyre sizing is derived from a tactical airlifter of comparable footprint requirement

assumptions.text: The integrated standby instrument annunciates a disagreement/failure against the primary displays such that its total or single-parameter loss is crew-evident.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the standby shares nothing with the primaries but does not describe a comparator or disagreement flag, so the Aware split for SF-011 is assumed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If no disagreement cue exists, more of SF-011's erroneous conditions move to the crew-Unaware row and the indication cells stay empty.

citations.quote: an independent standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.text: Loss of cabin/hold differential produces a crew alert via the avionics cabin-altitude channel, making sudden depressurisation crew-Aware while slow drift may not be.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists differential/cabin-altitude going to avionics and oxygen logic but does not state an explicit cabin-altitude warning threshold, forcing the Aware/Unaware split assumption for SF-012.
assumptions.ifWrong: If there is no cabin-altitude warning, the SF-012 slow-drift Unaware row expands to cover sudden loss too and the mitigation cell changes.

citations.quote: differential pressure and cabin altitude to the avionics and to the crew oxygen logic

assumptions.text: The two dissimilar lock sensing paths are sufficiently independent that a coincident common-mode error mis-reading both as locked is rare, keeping most SF-013 erroneous-indication cases crew-Aware.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD claims dissimilar, independently routed sensing but common-mode potential across both paths is a claim to be tested, not established, so the Aware placement is assumed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a common-mode defeats both paths, the SF-013 erroneous-lock condition belongs primarily on the Unaware row and the indication mitigation is weaker than stated.

citations.quote: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits

assumptions.text: Ice accretion on protected surfaces is not always self-evident from the flight deck, so an unannunciated loss of anti-ice protection can develop crew-Unaware.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes zone annunciation for electrical zones but does not confirm that all protection loss modes (e.g. bleed piccolo) are annunciated, forcing the Unaware row for SF-014.
assumptions.ifWrong: If every anti-ice loss mode is annunciated, the SF-014 Unaware row collapses into the Aware row and its indication cell fills.

citations.quote: Detection is advisory and automatic activation is available

assumptions.text: Individual element monitoring for SF-015 does not detect all air-data-corrupting heater loss modes, leaving an undetectable variant that develops crew-Unaware.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states elements are monitored individually but does not confirm the monitor covers partial degradation that still corrupts air data, so the Unaware row is assumed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If monitoring fully covers every heater-loss mode, the SF-015 Unaware row collapses into the Aware row.

citations.quote: windshields and the two ice detectors are electrically heated and are monitored individually

assumptions.text: The ice-detector, fire-detection-loop and restraint-tension-loop failures can develop with no annunciation of the sensing element's own health, justifying the crew-Unaware rows for SF-016, SF-017 and SF-020.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states detection/monitoring outputs (advisories, warnings, tension annunciations) but does not state whether the detectors/loops self-monitor and annunciate their own loss, so the undetectable variant cannot be dismissed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If each sensing path self-monitors and annunciates its own failure, the crew-Unaware rows for SF-016/017/020 collapse into the Aware rows and those failure conditions become detected.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-016 Unaware row, SF-017 Unaware row, SF-020 Unaware row

citations.quote: The restraint tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented loop and its coverage is a recorded item

assumptions.text: Fire/overheat detection and fire extinguishing (SF-017 total-loss and SF-018) may require a COMBINED condition — undetected fire together with unavailable extinguishing — to reach the worst outcome.
assumptions.rationale: ARP4761A Table A3 permits related sub-functions to require combined failure conditions; detect-and-extinguish are complementary sub-functions of 'Detect and suppress fire'. Flagging for the matrix Combined column.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the two are treated as independent single conditions only, the AFHA may understate the fire hazard; if combined, an additional combined FC row is needed.

citations.quote: detects fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected, and provides the means to extinguish

assumptions.text: Restraint tensioning (SF-019) and restraint-tension monitoring (SF-020) may require a COMBINED condition — undetected loss of tension while restraint has degraded — for the worst payload-shift outcome.
assumptions.rationale: SF-019 and SF-020 are complementary sub-functions of 'Restrain the payload'; the monitor being the only in-flight cue means a silent monitor plus a real tension loss combine. Flagging for the Combined column.
assumptions.ifWrong: If treated independently, the combined restraint-loss-plus-blind-monitor case is not captured and the AFHA may miss it.

citations.quote: In flight the crew has indication only; there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint

assumptions.text: The crew-Aware/Unaware split is deferred to the AFHA where indication and detection means are established; several indication/mitigation fields are left empty because the SDD grounds the output cue but not the crew procedure.
assumptions.rationale: The function list plus SDD ground the capability phrases and some output cues, but crew response procedures and detection thresholds are not stated at this stage.
assumptions.ifWrong: If procedures/detection thresholds differ from the assumed cues, the awareness tagging and mitigation fields need revision.
assumptions.usedFor: empty indication/mitigation fields across SF-016, SF-018, SF-020 rows

assumptions.text: Cylinder pressure is displayed continuously and low-pressure alerting exists, so the fully-depleted/failed-supply case is crew-Aware in flight but a mask/regulator fault manifesting only on donning is crew-Unaware.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states continuous pressure display and low-pressure alerting but does not state whether every downstream mask/regulator fault raises an alert, forcing the per-condition awareness split.
assumptions.ifWrong: If mask/regulator faults are alerted, the crew-Unaware rows collapse and only Aware rows remain; if depletion is NOT alerted below a threshold, the Total-loss Aware row must move to Unaware.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-021 Aware row (Total/Partial), SF-021 Unaware row (slow leak, donning failure, undetected off-spec oxygen)

citations.quote: Cylinder pressure is displayed continuously on the flight deck and is a dispatch item.
Oxygen to the four mask stations; cylinder pressure and system status to the flight deck; low pressure alerting.

assumptions.text: The two cylinders with crossover and per-mask independent regulators mean single-cylinder or single-regulator faults are partial-loss conditions rather than total loss.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes redundancy (crossover, independent per-mask regulators) but the FCIM must reflect which faults degrade versus eliminate supply; this shapes the partials[] entries.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the crossover or a single cylinder is the sizing limit, the 'reduced duration/reserve' partial would instead be a total-loss driver and the partial list changes.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-021 partials[] entries (reduced duration/reserve, loss to one or more mask stations)

citations.quote: Two cylinders with a crossover, either being capable of supplying the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve.
Regulators are independent per mask.

assumptions.text: No passenger/hold oxygen exists because the hold is unoccupied in flight, so the FCIM is bounded to crew supply only.
assumptions.rationale: The function is 'crew breathing oxygen'; the SDD confirms no passenger oxygen, so no occupant-oxygen failure conditions are authored.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any occupied-hold operation is later permitted, additional occupant-supply failure conditions would need to be added.
assumptions.usedFor: Scope bound of all SF-021 rows

citations.quote: There is no passenger oxygen: the hold is not occupied in flight.

assumptions.text: An erroneous or uncommanded primary-surface response about any single axis can reach a magnitude sufficient to cause loss of flight-path control before crew recovery.
assumptions.rationale: The function definition 'Control primary aerodynamic surfaces' states no authority limit, rate, or envelope-protection limiting, so the worst-case excursion is not bounded by the provided inputs.
