assumptions.ifWrong: If the two actuators are separable across zones, common-cause concern (2) in G-010/G-011 weakens and the co-location independence requirement can be relaxed.
assumptions.usedFor: G-010 finding (2), G-011 finding (2), and their co-location requirements

citations.quote: Every primary surface is driven by at least two actuators supplied from different hydraulic systems.

assumptions.text: HYD system C supplies an actuator in the roll surfaces on both the left and right sides, making it common to both branches of G-012.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD says ailerons are on B and C but does not explicitly state C feeds both left and right ailerons; inferred from C being a single aircraft-wide system serving ailerons.
assumptions.ifWrong: If HYD C only feeds one side's ailerons, the G-012 repeated-event modelling of HYD C is unnecessary and that common-cause contributor is removed.
assumptions.usedFor: G-012 finding (1) and the HYD C repeated-event requirement

citations.quote: C → elevators, ailerons

assumptions.text: The actuator control electronics (ACE) per surface is a shared node feeding both actuators of that surface, distinct from the dissimilar-FCC voting.
assumptions.rationale: The tree shows an ACE basic event and the SDD describes ACE but does not state whether the two actuators of one surface share one ACE.
assumptions.ifWrong: If each actuator has an independent ACE, common-cause concern (1) in G-010/G-011 weakens and the ACE independence requirement is already satisfied.

citations.quote: electrical power to the computers and to the actuator control electronics

assumptions.text: HYD C and HYD B do not share a common physical routing at the wing root (only A and B do).
assumptions.rationale: Needed to credit routing separation as a mitigating factor for the B/C independence in G-010/G-011.
assumptions.ifWrong: If C shares a run with B, the routing-separation mitigation in G-010/G-011 is void and a zonal common-cause contributor must be added.

citations.quote: Hydraulic system C run ... Routed separately from A and B along the opposite side

assumptions.text: The two aileron actuators in G-015 draw HYD B and HYD C (not the shared HYD A/B wing-root run), so that particular shared run does not directly couple this AND.
assumptions.rationale: The tree node names cite 'Aileron actuator (HYD B)' and 'Aileron actuator (HYD C)'; I inferred the AND is B–C rather than involving the A/B shared run.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a credited roll actuator draws HYD A/B via the shared wing-root run, G-015 gains an Installation-Design common-cause contributor and the mitigation/requirement set must add the A/B run.
assumptions.usedFor: G-015 findings row on routing; G-015 mitigation.

citations.quote: the ailerons from B and C

assumptions.text: The FCC detect-and-inhibit monitor is (or can be made) power- and partition-independent from the actuator command path it inhibits.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD asserts three FCCs on three sources but does not state whether monitor and command paths within the credited channel are separated.
assumptions.ifWrong: If monitor and command share the same source/partition, G-015 and G-016 AND independence is not assured and the derived requirements become mandatory pre-conditions.
assumptions.usedFor: G-015 and G-016 findings, requirements, verification notes.

citations.quote: Each computer is supplied from a different electrical source

assumptions.text: The FCC software dissimilarity argument (two teams) covers the vote/monitor logic and not only command generation.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states dissimilar software but does not scope which functions the dissimilarity spans.
assumptions.ifWrong: If dissimilarity does not span the monitor, a common software fault could both emit an erroneous yaw command and defeat its rejection, defeating G-016.
assumptions.usedFor: G-016 findings, requirement on dissimilarity coverage.

citations.quote: hosts software developed by one of two teams under a dissimilarity argument

assumptions.text: Mechanical reversion (stabiliser trim + lower rudder) requires neither FCC command nor the shared hydraulic supplies whose loss it backstops.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD calls reversion 'survivable but degraded' and says it results from loss of all electrical command paths, but does not confirm hydraulic independence of the reversion surfaces.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reversion depends on a hydraulic supply also credited in an axis branch, the G-022 top AND is weaker and reversion cannot be counted as the final diverse branch.
assumptions.usedFor: G-022 mechanical-reversion findings row, reversion requirement and verification.

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.text: FCC 2, mid equipment bay and the HYD/electrical crossings co-located in zone 300 create a credible single-zone common cause across multiple axis branches.
assumptions.rationale: The zonal model places FCC 2, mid equipment bay and HV/LV crossing points in zone 300; the SDD does not quantify separation there.
assumptions.ifWrong: If zone-300 separation is adequate, the particular-risk/zonal common-cause row in G-022 is downgraded and the associated ZSA finding closes without a new requirement.
assumptions.usedFor: G-022 environment/particular-risk findings row and ZSA verification note.

citations.quote: Mid hold (stations 4–6) ... mid equipment bay, FCC 2, HV/LV crossing points

assumptions.text: The FC-034 four-engine AND gate credits independent fuel feeds, so the single cross-feed gallery is treated as a common-cause contributor to that AND.
assumptions.rationale: The tree models per-engine 'loss of fuel at inlet' leaves under an AND but does not model the single-gallery coupling; the SDD states the gallery is the only cross-side path.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the AND already isolates each engine from the shared gallery, the G-027 gallery row overstates coupling and can be downgraded.
assumptions.usedFor: G-027 CMA rows; node 65 AND-gate independence

citations.quote: the only path by which fuel from one side reaches an engine on the other

assumptions.text: All four installed engines share a single part number and the four FADECs share a common design/software baseline.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names one selected turbofan type in the 330 kN class for all four positions but the model definition is not yet released, so common-design detail is not confirmed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a dissimilarity or lot-control argument exists, the common-design common-cause contributor to G-027 weakens and the associated independence requirement may be closed.

citations.quote: an existing certified high-bypass turbofan in the 330 kN class

assumptions.text: The reverser WoW inhibit on engines 2 and 3 is driven from the same LDG weight-on-wheels source rather than segregated per-reverser channels.
assumptions.rationale: The interface matrix shows a single WoW output feeding reversers among many consumers; the SDD does not state per-reverser WoW segregation or voting.
assumptions.ifWrong: If each inboard reverser has an independent WoW source/vote, the shared-WoW common cause between G-030 and G-031 disappears and those rows are downgraded.

citations.quote: Weight-on-wheels to reversers, pressurisation, restraint monitor, configuration

assumptions.text: The gate ids G-033/G-034/G-035 correspond to node ids 97, 101 and 106 respectively on the FC-054 fault-tree page.
assumptions.rationale: The project state exposes fault-tree nodes by numeric node id, not by G-0xx labels, so the mapping between the named gates and the tree nodes had to be inferred from node names.
assumptions.ifWrong: The CMA-to-gate links would attach to the wrong AND gate and must be re-pointed.
assumptions.usedFor: link actions and the subject fields of all three add_cma rows

citations.quote: downlock status is sensed by two independent proximity circuits per unit

assumptions.text: The free-fall alternate extension shares the same mechanical uplock/downlock release hardware as the normal HYD A path.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states uplocks/downlocks are mechanically held and hydraulically released but does not describe a separate release path for free-fall, so a shared release mechanism is the conservative reading.
assumptions.ifWrong: Concern (1) under G-034 is void and the HYD-A/free-fall independence claim strengthens, reducing the independence requirement.
assumptions.usedFor: G-034 findings concern (1) and its first requirement

citations.quote: Uplocks and downlocks are mechanically held and hydraulically released

assumptions.text: The two downlock proximity circuits use a common sensor type (dissimilarity is not claimed for the gear circuits, unlike the nose-door lock sensing).
assumptions.rationale: The SDD calls the gear circuits 'independent' but only calls the nose-door lock sensing 'dissimilar', so common type is the conservative reading for the gear circuits.
assumptions.ifWrong: Concern (1) under G-035 weakens and the type-defect common-mode requirement may be removed.
assumptions.usedFor: G-035 findings concern (1) and its second requirement

citations.quote: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits

assumptions.text: Node 106 is the AND gate asserting coincident misread of both downlock proximity circuits (G-036) on the FC-054 tree.
assumptions.rationale: The turn names G-036 by description but the project state exposes fault-tree nodes by numeric id; node 106 'Both independent downlock proximity …' is the AND matching the claim.
assumptions.ifWrong: The G-036 CMA link points at the wrong gate and must be re-linked to the correct AND node.

citations.quote: downlock status is sensed by two independent proximity circuits per unit

assumptions.text: Node 109 is the top AND asserting primary-and-standby coincident error (G-040) on the FC-069 tree.
assumptions.rationale: Node 109 'Undetected misleading standby indica…' is the top AND combining primary-error (110) with standby-error (113) branches, matching the claim.
assumptions.ifWrong: The G-040 CMA link points at the wrong gate and must be re-linked.

citations.quote: shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.text: Node 125 is the AND 'Spurious unlock command reaches actuator' combining spurious command (126) with interlock failure (127), i.e. G-043.
assumptions.rationale: The claim text matches node 125's name and children on the FC-078 (uncommanded unlock) tree.
assumptions.ifWrong: The G-043 CMA link points at the wrong gate and must be re-linked.

citations.quote: a pressure interlock vents and confirms residual differential below 0.1 psi

assumptions.text: The ECS-supplied pressure interlock signal and the NZD unlock command may share EPS/DC-essential power or door-control logic.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists ECS→NZD interlock and EPS as an all-systems supplier but does not state whether interlock sensing and unlock command have diverse supplies or separate logic.
assumptions.ifWrong: If they are already independent, the G-043 common-resource contributor and its independence requirements are unnecessary and the AND holds as drawn.

citations.quote: Residual differential below 0.1 psi as an interlock on the unlock command

assumptions.text: The two downlock proximity circuits' supply diversity and routing separation are not established by the SDD.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD asserts 'independent' circuits but gives no supply or routing detail, forcing the shared-supply / co-location exposure to remain open.
assumptions.ifWrong: If diverse supplies and separated routing are confirmed, the G-036 common-cause contributors are closed and the mitigation field can be filled.
assumptions.usedFor: G-036 findings, empty mitigation, requirements, node 106

citations.quote: two independent proximity circuits per unit

assumptions.text: G-044 is the top AND gate id 117 on the 'Uncommanded unlock / latch release' tree, G-047 is the top AND gate id 128 on the 'Undetected erroneous lock indication' tree, and G-048 is the 'Visor drive fails to close door' AND gate id 137 on the nose-pressure-boundary tree.
assumptions.rationale: The turn names gates G-044/G-047/G-048 by title but the project state exposes fault-tree nodes only by numeric id; I matched titles to node ids to set the CMA-to-gate links.
assumptions.ifWrong: The link actions attach the CMA rows to the wrong gates and must be re-pointed to the correct node ids.

citations.quote: Uncommanded / erroneous unlock command

assumptions.text: The eight lock pins, twelve latches, lock actuator and both sensing paths are physically located within or transit zone 110 (nose visor structure), making a zone-110 particular risk a credible common cause across the pin/latch and sensing AND branches.
assumptions.rationale: The zonal model lists zone 110 as housing 'visor latches, lock pins, lock actuator and sensing harness'; exact intra-zone separation between the two restraints is not given.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the pin and latch restraints are in fact separated into distinct zones/compartments, the zone-110 common-cause concern in G-044/G-047 weakens or drops.
assumptions.usedFor: CMA findings for G-044 and G-047

citations.quote: Visor latches, lock pins, lock actuator, sensing harness

assumptions.text: The electric backup visor drive is fed from an electrical bus that is not lost simultaneously with HYD A, so HYD A loss does not also disable the backup.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the backup is electric but does not identify which bus feeds it, so the independence of the HYD-A/electric AND cannot be confirmed from the document.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the backup drive's electrical supply is coupled to HYD A (e.g. shares the same generator/EDP engine), the G-048 AND is not genuinely independent and the closure claim overstates protection.

citations.quote: opened and closed hydraulically from system A with an electric backup drive

assumptions.text: The lock-pin actuator's 'separate hydraulic supply' is fully independent of the HYD A visor drive up to and including its source, not merely a separate branch off HYD A.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply but does not name which hydraulic system feeds the pins, so full source independence cannot be confirmed from the inputs.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the pin supply shares a source with the latch/visor HYD A path, the G-052 latch/pin AND collapses toward a single-hydraulic common cause and the independence claim (and any DAL reduction resting on it) fails.
assumptions.usedFor: G-052 CMA row — Common Resources (hydraulic) concern and its independence requirement

citations.quote: Eight independent locking pins are then driven … by a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply

assumptions.text: The AC and DC feeds to the heated air-data elements converge on the common four-generator EPS such that an EPS-level event is a credible common cause across the AND inputs.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD says the elements are electrically heated and that EPS supplies every consumer, but does not give the specific bus allocation of AC vs DC heater feeds.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the AC and DC feeds are genuinely segregated to independent sources with no common-mode failure, the G-054 electrical common-resource concern weakens and fewer independence requirements are needed.
assumptions.usedFor: G-054 CMA row — Common Resources (electrical) and DC-essential concerns

citations.quote: The electrical system generates, converts, stores and distributes power to every consumer on the aircraft

assumptions.text: The two aft-zone fire-detection loops are the same detection technology/design, making them susceptible to a common design/material deficiency.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes dual-loop continuous detection but does not state whether the two loops are dissimilar; NASA-FTH treats identical redundant active elements as common-cause susceptible.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the two loops are dissimilar in technology, the common-design contributor under G-058 is materially reduced and the detection AND independence is stronger.
assumptions.usedFor: G-058 CMA row — Development/Design identical-loop concern and the CCF-contributor requirement

citations.quote: dual-loop continuous fire detection, with the two loops routed separately and an AND logic between them

assumptions.text: The 'DC essential supply loss to FPR detection' event (node 165) represents a resource common to both the detection loops and the loop-fault BITE/annunciation, making it a genuine common-cause across the FC-099 top AND.
assumptions.rationale: The tree already models node 165 under the annunciation branch, but the SDD states detection is DC-ess supplied without confirming the BITE and loops share a single feed vs. segregated feeds.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detection and annunciation draw from segregated DC-ess feeds, concern (1) in the G-060 CMA weakens and the top-AND independence is stronger than stated.
assumptions.usedFor: G-060 CMA concern (1); node 165 repeated-event treatment

citations.quote: DC power from the essential bus to detection and from the hot battery bus to the discharge circuits

assumptions.text: The FC-122 cross-comparison monitor (node 175) draws its comparands from the same ADIRU/air-data references that generate the displayed value, so a source-common error is not caught by reference-to-reference comparison.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes three reference units and cross-comparison but does not state whether the monitor's inputs are architecturally distinct from the generation path's inputs.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the monitor uses a genuinely independent sensing/derivation path, concern (1) in the G-065 CMA no longer defeats the AND and the independence holds.
assumptions.usedFor: G-065 CMA concern (1); node 175/166 top-AND independence

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data.

assumptions.text: The two fire/overheat detection loops in a given zone, though separately clipped on opposite sides, share the same fire-zone environment such that the fire being detected is a credible common cause across the FC-099 detection branch.
assumptions.rationale: SDD 5.12.5 asserts separate routing but does not state the loops are qualified to survive the fire condition long enough for at least one to signal.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loop separation/fire-hardening is qualified against the design fire, concern (2) in the G-060 CMA is mitigated rather than open.

citations.quote: The two detection loops for each zone are routed on opposite sides of that zone and are separately clipped.

praData.threat: Tire burst / flailing tread release (retractable wheeled gear; §25.734 / AC 25.734-1)
praData.desc: Burst or tread release from the twenty-tyre gear (six three-wheel main bogies, three per side, zones 710/720; twin-wheel nose unit zone 730). Debris/tread flails within the gear bay; the SDD records brake hydraulic lines A and B running through each main gear bay in 'adjacent but separately clipped bundles' with steering and brake harnesses — a recorded zonal co-location. A single burst reaching both bundles in one bay is the credible common cause defeating the dual-brake-supply independence. Debris size / energy / trajectory not asserted — requires AC 25.734-1 threat model.
praData.systems: LDG (brake lines A/B, steering & brake harnesses, tyres); HYD A and B (brake hydraulic supply); FCS via HYD A/B wing-root run only if propagation established
praData.csfl: Co-located brake hydraulic lines A and B in a single main gear bay: a burst severing both defeats the normal(B)/alternate(A) brake independence, a common cause across otherwise-independent supplies.
praData.mitigation:
Separately clipped and shielded A/B brake bundles within each bay (SDD 5.6.5); accumulator-supported emergency braking sized to six full applications with all three hydraulic systems lost (SDD 5.4.3); anti-skid per wheel pair. Proposed outcome: MINIMISED pending debris-trajectory substantiation.
Proposed requirements: • The LDG installation shall route brake hydraulic lines A and B in each main gear bay such that no single credible tyre-burst debris trajectory can sever both.
• The LDG installation shall shield the steering and brake electrical harnesses in each gear bay against tyre-burst debris such that a single burst does not disable both anti-skid and braking on that side.
aiFunctions: SF-008 Support the aircraft and absorb ground loads
aiRequirements: The LDG installation shall route brake hydraulic lines A and B in each main gear bay such that no single credible tyre-burst debris trajectory can sever both.

The LDG installation shall shield the steering and brake electrical harnesses in each gear bay against tyre-burst debris such that a single burst does not disable both anti-skid and braking on that side.

praData.threat: Tire burst affecting complete loss of wheel braking (FC-044)
praData.desc: Failure condition FC-044 — complete loss of wheel braking capability — as reachable by a single tyre-burst common cause severing co-located A and B brake hydraulic lines in one main gear bay. On a semi-prepared 1,800 m strip against ~1,080 m predicted rollout, loss of wheel braking erodes the operating margin the SDD identifies as the basis of the braking design.
praData.systems: LDG (wheel braking); HYD A and B brake supply
praData.csfl: A/B brake line co-location in the gear bay (SDD-recorded zonal item) is the single cause defeating normal/alternate brake independence for FC-044.
praData.mitigation:
Accumulator emergency braking (six applications, all systems lost); reverse thrust on the two inboard engines (SF-005) as an independent deceleration means; separately clipped/shielded bundles. Proposed outcome: MINIMISED pending substantiation.
Proposed requirements: • The braking architecture shall retain a deceleration means independent of a single gear-bay event sufficient to stop within the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing-distance requirement.
aiRequirements: The braking architecture shall retain a deceleration means independent of a single gear-bay event sufficient to stop within the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing-distance requirement.

praData.desc: Forward-facing bird strike on the nose visor structure (110), flight-deck windshields (130), forward-fuselage probes/ports and ice detectors, and the four engine inlets (610–640). Windshield/probe strike bears on air-data and pitot/static/AoA integrity; engine ingestion bears on thrust. Two ice detectors of the same type on opposite sides of the forward fuselage are both exposed to a forward strike (commonality recorded as an item). Impact energy / bird mass per §33.76 and structural penetration threshold not asserted — analyst inputs.
praData.systems: AVI (probes/ports, air-data via ADIRU); NZD/structure (nose visor); IPS (two same-type ice detectors, probe heating); PRP (engine inlet ingestion, four engines)
praData.csfl: Common same-type ice detectors on the forward fuselage are both exposed to a single forward strike; probe/port co-location on forward-facing surfaces is a candidate common cause for air-data corruption.
praData.mitigation:
Four engines podded and separated in left/right zones limits multi-engine ingestion from a single strike; three ADIRUs (two main bus, one DC essential) and an independent standby instrument sharing no sensor/processing preserve air-data after a single probe loss (SDD 5.11); windshield protection per §25.775. Proposed outcome: MINIMISED pending bird-mass/energy substantiation.
Proposed requirements: • The forward-fuselage air-data sensing (probes, ports, AoA) shall be installed such that a single bird strike within the §33.76 / §25.631 threat envelope cannot corrupt all air-data reference sources.
• The two ice detectors shall be sited such that a single forward bird strike cannot disable both.
aiFunctions: SF-009 Present flight and navigation information
SF-015 Heat probes, ports and windshields
aiRequirements: The forward-fuselage air-data sensing (probes, ports, AoA) shall be installed such that a single bird strike within the §33.76 / §25.631 threat envelope cannot corrupt all air-data reference sources.
The two ice detectors shall be sited such that a single forward bird strike cannot disable both.

praData.threat: Bird strike affecting misleading flight information (FC-055)
praData.desc: Failure condition FC-055 — misleading flight information displayed — as reachable by a bird strike corrupting forward-fuselage air-data sensing (probes/ports/AoA) feeding the ADIRUs and displays. Crew-aware erroneous flight data case.
praData.csfl: Forward-facing probe/port co-location: a single strike corrupting common sensing defeats reference-source diversity for FC-055.
praData.mitigation: Three ADIRUs with dissimilar bus supply; independent standby instrument on DC essential sharing no sensor or processing (SDD 5.11.2/5.11.3); cross-comparison monitoring. Proposed outcome: MINIMISED pending substantiation.
aiFunctions: SF-009 Present flight and navigation information

praData.threat: Bird strike affecting engine thrust (FC-032 / FC-033)
praData.desc: Failure condition FC-032 (partial loss of thrust, symmetric) and FC-033 (loss of thrust one side producing asymmetry) as reachable by bird ingestion into one or more of the four engine inlets. The outboard 28 m moment arm makes a single-outboard ingestion the directional-control sizing case.
praData.mitigation: Four engines podded and separated left/right; continue-to-suitable-aerodrome after loss of any one engine at/after V1 (SDD 5.1.3); rudder authority sized to the outboard-engine-out case. Proposed outcome: MINIMISED pending §33.76 ingestion substantiation.

praData.threat: Lightning strike (§25.1316 / AC 20-136B) — direct attachment and conducted/indirect effects
praData.desc: Direct lightning attachment to extremities (wingtips 510/520, nacelles 610-640, empennage 800, nose visor 110) with conducted transients and induced coupling onto the six EWS routes. Zone-spanning routings that carry the coupled transient into avionics/FCS bays: HV feeder left/right (610/620,530,300,200), LV signal left/right (120,200,300,400,800), data network channels 1&2 (120,200,300,400,800), fuel feed gallery through the wing box (510,530,300,540,520). Fuel tanks in 510/520 are a lightning ignition-source concern (fuel-tank ignition prevention, §25.981, not substantiated by the SDD). Study is at drawing/model stage: bundle build and clamping positions are preliminary.
praData.systems: FCS, AVI, EPS, FUE, PRP, EWS
praData.csfl: Coupled lightning transient is a common-cause candidate across the three dissimilar flight control computers (bays 120/300/400) and the two data network channels, which the SDD claims 'share no connector or penetration' — that independence claim must survive a lightning indirect-effects common-mode check rather than be assumed. Simultaneous corruption of primary displays and reference units feeding both would defeat the display/reference redundancy.
praData.mitigation:
Bond and divert direct attachment via structure/diverter provision at extremities; shield and twist the LV/data routes; maintain HV/LV route separation with the two mid-bay crossing points shielded (§5.14.2); transient protection at avionics/FCS interfaces; fuel-tank ignition prevention on the wing-box gallery. Survivability claim: SHOWN TO BE ACCEPTABLE contingent on lightning zoning, transient-level substantiation and §25.981 evidence — asserted at model stage only.
Proposed requirements: • The aircraft shall protect the three flight control computers and the two data network channels against lightning indirect effects such that no single lightning event corrupts more than one flight-control command path.
• The fuel system shall prevent lightning-induced ignition sources within the wing-box tanks and cross-feed gallery per §25.981.
aiRequirements: The aircraft shall protect the three flight control computers and the two data network channels against lightning indirect effects such that no single lightning event corrupts more than one flight-control command path.
The fuel system shall prevent lightning-induced ignition sources within the wing-box tanks and cross-feed gallery per §25.981.

praData.threat: High-Intensity Radiated Fields (§25.1317 / AC 20-158A) — external RF illumination coupling to electrical/electronic systems
praData.desc: External RF field illuminates the airframe and couples onto the six EWS routes and into equipment bays housing electronic systems: FCC1/forward avionics (120), flight deck displays/standby instrument (130), FCC2/mid equipment bay (300), FCC3/aft equipment bay (400), nose door lock sensing harness (110,120,130). Coupling paths are the LV signal routes and the two data network channels (120,200,300,400,800). HIRF is a whole-airframe illumination, not a localised zone event, so all bays hosting flight-critical electronics are in scope. Study is at drawing/model stage: bundle build and clamping positions are preliminary.
praData.csfl: HIRF is an inherently common-cause threat: a single external field illuminates all three flight control computers, all three air-data inertial reference units and both data network channels simultaneously, so the dissimilarity/triplex redundancy of FCS and AVI does not by itself defeat it. The independent standby instrument (DC essential bus, 'shares no supply, no sensor and no processing') and the nose-door dual dissimilar lock sensing must each demonstrate HIRF immunity independently.
praData.mitigation:
Airframe/equipment-bay shielding effectiveness, harness shield termination and bundle segregation per EWS routing, and equipment-level HIRF qualification to the AC 20-158A environment for flight-critical and essential functions; verify the standby-instrument and lock-sensing independence claims survive HIRF illumination. Survivability claim: SHOWN TO BE ACCEPTABLE contingent on HIRF environment definition, shielding-effectiveness substantiation and equipment qualification — asserted at model stage only, not verified.
Proposed requirements: • Flight-critical and essential electronic systems (FCS, AVI, standby indication, nose-door lock sensing) shall meet the AC 20-158A HIRF environment without loss or malfunction of function.
• The independent standby instrument shall retain valid attitude, airspeed and altitude under HIRF illumination independently of the primary display chain.
aiRequirements: Flight-critical and essential electronic systems (FCS, AVI, standby indication, nose-door lock sensing) shall meet the AC 20-158A HIRF environment without loss or malfunction of function.
The independent standby instrument shall retain valid attitude, airspeed and altitude under HIRF illumination independently of the primary display chain.

praData.threat: Hail / ice impact on forward-facing structures and inlets (external environmental, forward trajectory)
praData.desc: Hail impacts forward-facing surfaces: the nose visor (zone 110), flight-deck windshields (130), wing leading edges (510/520) and the four engine inlets (610–640). Model as impact energy on windshields, radome/visor skin, leading-edge structure, probes/ports, ice detectors and engine fan/inlet. Air-data probes and the two same-type ice detectors on the forward fuselage are struck directly. Cross-zone: none unique to hail beyond the direct forward strike; the ice-detector commonality (identical type, opposite sides of forward fuselage) means a single frontal hail encounter can degrade both detectors simultaneously — a common-cause across the nominally redundant detection pair. Survivability: windshield and structural strength are substantiated by structural analysis / test (§25.775, §25.631), not asserted here; engine hail ingestion tolerance is an engine-type §33.78 matter. Functional counterpart: probe/port corruption feeds FC-089 (undetected loss of probe/port heating corrupting air data) analog via air-data path, and simultaneous ice-detector degradation feeds SF-016 detection FCs; ingestion could contribute to FC-032/FC-033 thrust FCs. Claim: effects MINIMISED by structural substantiation and probe/detector redundancy where it survives; the same-type ice-detector common-cause is SHOWN-TO-BE-ACCEPTABLE only if a frontal encounter cannot defeat both — that must be substantiated, not assumed.
praData.systems: AVI (air data / ice detection), IPS (ice detectors, probe heat), FCS (windshield/structure interfaces), PRP (engine inlet ingestion), NZD (visor skin as forward structure)

praData.threat: In-flight ice accretion and ice shedding on airframe surfaces, inlets and probes (environmental; refine to type-design ice envelope)
praData.desc: Ice accretes on unprotected/under-protected surfaces where anti-ice is lost or degraded: wing and engine-cowl leading edges (510/520, 610–640) protected by cross-bleed hot air; stabiliser leading edges (800) protected by six electrically-heated zones; probes, static ports, windshields and the two ice detectors (forward fuselage, zones 120/130 region) electrically heated. Shed ice from wing/inlet can be ingested by the podded engines beneath the high wing. Cross-zone propagation via routing: wing anti-ice ducting shares the wing leading edge with the outboard electrical route behind a shielded partition (510/540→510/520 per §4) — a duct rupture or the electrical route are co-located, so an ice-protection bleed-duct event is also a zonal/electrical concern; the cross-bleed manifold in zone 300 joins both sides, so a manifold fault removes bleed anti-ice from BOTH wings/cowls at once, defeating the 'available from either side' redundancy claim. Functional counterpart: loss of airframe/inlet anti-ice → FC-086 (complete loss of airframe surface and engine-inlet anti-ice); loss on one side/zone → FC-084/FC-085; undetected probe/port heating loss corrupting air data → FC-089; windshield heating loss → FC-088; erroneous/undetected anti-ice loss → FC-082. Same-type ice-detector commonality is a common-cause that can leave accretion undetected → SF-016 detection FCs. Survivability: aircraft must fly the certification icing envelope; effects MINIMISED by bleed cross-feed and independent electrical zones where redundancy survives, but the cross-bleed manifold common node and the identical-detector pair are common-cause contributors that must be reflected in the FC-086 and detection fault trees rather than left out.
praData.systems: IPS (bleed & electrical anti-ice, ice detectors, probe/windshield heat), ECS (cross-bleed manifold, bleed source), AVI (air data corruption, ice-detection display), PRP (inlet anti-ice, shed-ice ingestion)
praData.csfl: Cross-bleed manifold in zone 300 is a single node joining both sides — a manifold fault removes bleed anti-ice from both wings and both cowl groups simultaneously; the two same-type ice detectors are a common-cause across the detection redundancy.

praData.threat: Cabin / cargo / compartment fire in flight (in-flight fire and smoke — §25.831(c) smoke evacuation, §25.855 cargo/baggage compartment fire protection)
praData.desc: In-flight fire or overheat originating in (a) the hold stations 200/300/400 — smoke detection at nine stations, NO suppression fitted, a deliberate recorded decision because the hold carries a single blade and no combustible palletised load; (b) an engine nacelle 610–640 or the APU compartment within zone 800 — designated fire zones with dual-loop continuous detection and extinguishing; (c) the forward equipment bay 120, which co-locates the two crew-oxygen cylinders (an oxidiser/high-pressure source) with FCC 1 and the forward avionics racks; and (d) smoke migration into the occupied flight deck 130. The hold-suppression omission is the load-bearing survivability item recorded in the SDD as an assumption to be substantiated.
praData.systems: FPR (dual-loop nacelle/APU detection, two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed, hold smoke detection with no suppression, bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat detection); OXY (two HP gaseous cylinders in forward equipment bay 120 — oxidiser source); CRG (restraint tension monitoring loop and winches in the hold); FCS (FCC 1 in zone 120, FCC 2 in zone 300, FCC 3 in zone 400 — fire in a hold equipment bay threatens a flight-control computer); EWS (left-side low-voltage signal route and the restraint loop share the hold zones and can carry fire effects between them)
praData.csfl: A hold fire in a mid/aft equipment bay (300 houses FCC 2; 400 houses FCC 3; 120 houses FCC 1) is a common-source threat to the fly-by-wire independence claim — the three dissimilar flight control computers are installed in three separate bays precisely so no single event takes more than one, but a fire in one bay defeats that bay's computer and, if smoke/heat propagates along the shared left-side electrical route or the full-length restraint loop through 200/300/400, could reach a second. In the forward equipment bay 120 the oxygen cylinders co-located with FCC 1 and avionics racks are an oxidiser that can intensify a local electrical fire.
praData.mitigation:
Hold: nine-station smoke detection annunciated to the crew alerting system; no combustible palletised load carried (single blade); NO suppression fitted (recorded decision, to be substantiated). Nacelle/APU: dual-loop continuous detection with AND warning logic degrading to single-loop, two extinguisher bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed either bottle to either nacelle, independent APU bottle with automatic ground discharge, discharge circuits on the hot battery bus so they survive total generation loss. Overheat detection on bleed-duct runs and main gear bays. Portable extinguishers at flight deck and hold access door. Detection powered from DC essential bus. Survivability claim: hold-fire effect MINIMISED by detection plus absence of combustible load; nacelle/APU fire effect SHOWN-TO-BE-ACCEPTABLE by dual detection and cross-plumbed extinguishing — both claims remain conditional on the recorded no-hold-suppression assumption being substantiated.
Proposed requirements: • A means shall be provided to substantiate that a fire in the unoccupied hold, with smoke detection but no suppression, does not progress to a hazardous or catastrophic condition before the crew can execute an emergency descent and land (§25.855 substantiation of the recorded no-suppression decision).
• The installation shall demonstrate that a fire in any single equipment bay (120, 300 or 400) cannot, by direct effect or by smoke/heat propagation along the shared left-side electrical route or the full-length restraint tension monitoring loop through zones 200/300/400, defeat more than one flight control computer (preserve the three-bay FCC independence claim).
• The forward equipment bay 120 installation shall demonstrate that a fire involving the co-located crew-oxygen cylinders, FCC 1 and the avionics racks is contained such that the oxygen cylinders do not act as an oxidiser intensifying a bay fire (separation/segregation of the HP oxygen source from ignition sources per §25.855/§25.869).
aiFunctions: SF-018 Extinguish engine and APU fires
SF-001 Control primary aerodynamic surfaces (FCC bays 120/300/400 threatened by an equipment-bay fire)
SF-019 Restrain and tension the payload longitudinally
SF-021 Supply crew breathing oxygen (cylinders in zone 120 are a fire/oxidiser item)
aiRequirements: A means shall be provided to substantiate that a fire in the unoccupied hold, with smoke detection but no suppression, does not progress to a hazardous or catastrophic condition before the crew can execute an emergency descent and land (§25.855 substantiation of the recorded no-suppression decision).

The installation shall demonstrate that a fire in any single equipment bay (120, 300 or 400) cannot, by direct effect or by smoke/heat propagation along the shared left-side electrical route or the full-length restraint tension monitoring loop through zones 200/300/400, defeat more than one flight control computer (preserve the three-bay FCC independence claim).

The forward equipment bay 120 installation shall demonstrate that a fire involving the co-located crew-oxygen cylinders, FCC 1 and the avionics racks is contained such that the oxygen cylinders do not act as an oxidiser intensifying a bay fire (separation/segregation of the HP oxygen source from ignition sources per §25.855/§25.869).

zsaData.desc: Nose visor structure — unpressurised when open, pressure boundary when closed; houses visor latches, lock pins, lock actuator and sensing harness.
zsaData.equip: Twelve rotary latches on common torque shaft, eight locking pins, lock actuator, proximity sensing harness
zsaData.interference: Common torque shaft is a single mechanical path across twelve latches; lock sensing harness transits 110/120/130 opposite door actuation power at two separated bulkhead penetrations.
zsaData.mitigation: Eight independent pins driven by separate actuator on separate hydraulic supply prevent latch back-drive; dual dissimilar independently-routed lock sensing; pressure interlock <0.1 psi in series with unlock. Verify torque-shaft common-cause and penetration separation.

zsaData.desc: Forward equipment bay — pressurised, conditioned; houses FCC 1, oxygen cylinders and forward avionics racks.
zsaData.equip: Flight control computer 1, two HP crew-oxygen cylinders, forward avionics racks
zsaData.interference: Gaseous oxygen cylinders co-located with electrical avionics racks and FCC 1 in one bay; low-voltage signal and data channel 1 routes transit this zone.
zsaData.mitigation: Cylinders installed outside any zone containing a high-energy electrical source per SDD; thermal discharge indicator overboard. Verify O2 cylinder separation from FCC 1 / avionics energy sources and material compatibility.

zsaData.desc: Flight deck — pressurised, occupied; houses displays, inceptors, standby instrument, fire handles and crew oxygen masks.

zsaData.mitigation: Standby instrument wired directly to DC essential on route independent of primary display feeders. Verify installation preserves the shared-nothing standby independence claim within the zone.

zsaData.desc: Forward hold, stations 1–3 — low differential, unoccupied; houses saddles 1–3, restraint straps, tension loop and smoke detectors.
zsaData.equip: Saddles 1–3 with two straps each, restraint tension monitoring loop, smoke detectors

zsaData.mitigation: Loss of any one strap carried by neighbours; two-adjacent-station loss annunciated. No-suppression decision recorded as assumption to substantiate. Verify tension loop / fuel-vent / electrical co-location separation.

zsaData.desc: Mid hold, stations 4–6 — low differential, unoccupied; houses saddles 4–6, mid equipment bay, FCC 2 and HV/LV crossing points.
zsaData.equip: Saddles 4–6, mid equipment bay, FCC 2, HV/LV feeder crossing points
zsaData.interference: Convergence zone: HYD A+B wing-root run, HYD C run, fuel cross-feed gallery, brake lines A/B, HV feeders, LV signal, both data channels, and bleed cross-bleed manifold all transit here; the only two HV-to-LV crossing points on the aircraft are in this bay.
zsaData.mitigation: HV/LV separation replaced by shielding and defined minimum distance at the two crossings. Multiple recorded installation items converge here — each AND-independence claim (A/B hydraulics, dual data, HV/LV) must be tested by common-mode analysis and any coupling reflected as a common-cause contributor.
housedFunctions: Restrain and tension the payload longitudinally

zsaData.desc: Aft hold, stations 7–9 — low differential, unoccupied; houses saddles 7–9, aft equipment bay and FCC 3.
zsaData.interference: FCC 3 installed here; HYD C run, LV signal and data channels transit the zone; tension loop continues full length.
zsaData.mitigation: Three FCCs deliberately split across forward/mid/aft bays for zonal independence. Verify FCC 3 installation and routing separation from HYD C.

zsaData.desc: Left wing box and leading edge — flammable fluid present; houses fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting and outboard electrical route.
zsaData.equip: Left outboard/mid/inboard fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery segment, wing anti-ice piccolo ducting, outboard electrical route
zsaData.interference: Hot bleed anti-ice ducting shares the leading edge with the outboard electrical route inside a flammable-fluid zone; fuel cross-feed gallery transits.
zsaData.mitigation: Anti-ice ducting and outboard electrical route separated by a shielded partition along the full run; vent/surge lines outboard of all electrical harnesses. Verify partition integrity and ignition-source control in a flammable zone.
housedFunctions: Anti-ice airframe surfaces and engine inlets

zsaData.desc: Right wing box and leading edge — flammable fluid present; mirror of 510; houses fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting and outboard electrical route.

zsaData.mitigation: Shielded partition full run; refuel point with independent overflow protection. Verify partition and ignition-source control.

zsaData.desc: Left wing root — pressure boundary transit; houses HYD A and B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration and HV feeder transit.
zsaData.equip: HYD A and HYD B wing-root run, left bleed duct penetration, left HV feeder
zsaData.interference: Recorded installation item: HYD systems A and B share this wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary — a direct coupling of two nominally independent hydraulic systems. HV feeder and bleed duct also transit.
zsaData.mitigation: SDD keeps duct routing clear of HV feeder with minimum separation; A/B share a wing-root run flagged as a dedicated zonal item. This shared run defeats A/B independence and must be entered in the affected fault trees as a common-cause contributor per ARP4761A CMA.

zsaData.desc: Right wing root — pressure boundary transit; mirror of 530; houses HYD A and B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration and HV feeder transit.

zsaData.mitigation: Same as 530 mirrored; A/B commonality is a recorded installation item requiring CMA. Verify pressure-boundary penetration separation.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 1 (left outboard) — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone; houses engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, fire detection loops and extinguisher plumbing.
zsaData.equip: Turbofan engine 1, dual-channel FADEC, 150 kVA generator, engine-driven hydraulic pump (HYD A), dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Fire zone with high-energy rotating machinery and flammable fluid; HV feeder and bleed duct originate here and transit 620/530/300/200. Uncontained rotor/engine burst can release debris beyond the nacelle.
zsaData.mitigation: Dual-loop continuous detection routed on opposite sides with AND logic; two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed; left/right services not commingled outboard of wing root. Bearing PRAs: rotor burst, engine burst, nacelle fire, bird/hail/ice on inlet.

zsaData.mitigation: Rudder segment runs on opposite sides of aft fuselage; stabiliser heater feeders on opposite side from rudder runs; APU dual-loop detection with automatic ground discharge unattended. Bearing PRAs: engine/APU burst, APU fire.

cmaData.subject: G-001 Erroneous voted pitch command from flight control computers (FC-001)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Three dissimilar FCCs, each on a different electrical source, in three separate bays, hosting software from one of two teams, vote on command.. The three flight control computers fail independently, so a single common cause does not drive all three to vote the same erroneous pitch command.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
Common Resources (electrical): each FCC on a different electrical source per SDD §5.3.2 — supports independence, but all rely on EPS as a shared resource and the DC essential bus feeds FCC-related loads. | Loss/corruption of a shared bus could couple channels. | SDD claims different source per computer; verify bus assignment leaves no common feed.
Development/Design (software): dissimilarity argument rests on only TWO teams for THREE computers, so at least two channels share a software team. | A design/coding error common to the shared-team channels could produce a correlated erroneous command that the third does not catch, weakening the 2-of-3 vote. | Dissimilarity across two teams only — partial; a same-team error defeats two of three.
Development/Design (hardware): three computers may share a common part or common ADIRU input processing. | Common hardware fault correlates channels. | SDD states 'three dissimilar flight control computers' — dissimilarity claimed but not substantiated here.
Installation Design (co-location): FCC1 in fwd equip bay (120), FCC2 in mid hold (300), FCC3 in aft hold (400) — physically separated. | Separation supports independence; a single zonal event does not take all three. | Three separate bays per SDD §5.3.5 — supports the claim.
Common Resources (data/input): all three vote on the same air-data/inertial inputs. | A common erroneous input drives all three to the same wrong-but-consistent command (see G-003). | Shared input is a genuine coupling; addressed under G-003.
cmaData.mitigation:
Substantiate the FCC dissimilarity argument (dissimilar hardware and the two-team software split) and confirm no shared electrical bus, no shared input-processing lane defeats the 2-of-3 vote; require zonal separation of the three bays be maintained.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The FCC set shall be shown by dissimilarity analysis to have no single design or software error capable of producing a common erroneous pitch command across the voting majority.
• Each FCC shall be supplied from an independent electrical source such that no single bus loss affects more than one channel.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Three dissimilar FCCs, each on a different electrical source, in three separate bays, hosting software from one of two teams, vote on command.
aiRequirements: The FCC set shall be shown by dissimilarity analysis to have no single design or software error capable of producing a common erroneous pitch command across the voting majority.
Each FCC shall be supplied from an independent electrical source such that no single bus loss affects more than one channel.

cmaData.subject: G-003 Erroneous air-data / inertial input driving valid but wrong pitch (FC-001)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Three air data inertial reference units (two on main buses, one on DC essential) with FCC input monitoring cross-checking references.. The ADIRU/air-data source error and the FCC input-monitoring failure are independent, so an erroneous input is rejected before it drives an erroneous but consistent pitch command.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
Common Resources (sensors): common pitot/static/angle-of-attack sensing feeding the reference units. | A common sensing error (e.g. blocked/iced probes) corrupts multiple ADIRUs identically, presenting a consistent-but-wrong input the monitor cannot reject by comparison. | Probe/port heating exists (SF-015) but its loss is a recognised common-cause on air data — shared sensing defeats cross-comparison.
Environment (icing/mechanical): forward-fuselage probes exposed to a common icing or hail environment. | Simultaneous corruption of redundant air-data channels. | PRA icing / probe-heat coverage relevant; a shared environmental threat couples the sources.
Development/Design (software): ADIRUs of a common type share input-processing logic. | Common computation error yields correlated erroneous data. | SDD does not state ADIRU dissimilarity — commonality of type is a potential coupling.
Common Resources (electrical): two ADIRUs on main buses, one on DC essential — partial diversity. | Loss of a shared bus reduces available references for the monitor. | Split supply (2 main + 1 essential) supports partial independence per SDD §5.11.2.
Development/Design (monitor independence): the FCC input monitor consumes the same air-data it is meant to police. | If the input is consistent across sources, the monitor has nothing to vote against and passes the error. | The monitor is not independent of a common-mode sensing error — this is the load-bearing weakness of the AND gate.
cmaData.mitigation:
Establish air-data source independence to the sensing level (dissimilar/separated probes, robust probe heating) and provide an inertial or independent cross-check the monitor can use when air-data sources agree erroneously.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The FCC input monitoring shall detect and reject an erroneous air-data/inertial input using at least one reference independent of the common pitot/static/AoA sensing chain.
• Probe and port heating serving the air-data sensing chain shall be shown adequate to prevent common icing-induced corruption of the redundant references.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Three air data inertial reference units (two on main buses, one on DC essential) with FCC input monitoring cross-checking references.
aiRequirements: The FCC input monitoring shall detect and reject an erroneous air-data/inertial input using at least one reference independent of the common pitot/static/AoA sensing chain.
Probe and port heating serving the air-data sensing chain shall be shown adequate to prevent common icing-induced corruption of the redundant references.

cmaData.subject: G-005 Uncommanded elevator motion not arrested (FC-002)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Each primary surface driven by at least two actuators on different hydraulic systems (elevators on A and C), with FCC vote/monitor arresting an uncommanded runaway.. The elevator actuator runaway/hardover and the FCC vote/monitor failure to detect and arrest it are independent, so a single cause does not both drive the surface and blind the monitor.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
Common Resources (electrical): actuator control electronics and the FCC monitor may share a power feed. | A shared supply loss could disable the arresting monitor while the actuator drives. | Verify the monitor path and actuator control electronics do not share a single bus.
Development/Design (actuator control electronics): a fault in the actuator control electronics could both command motion and corrupt the feedback the monitor uses. | The monitor is fed by the same electronics it must police, so a single ACE fault defeats both legs of the AND. | Elevators on two hydraulic systems (A and C) support force independence, but electrical command/monitor commonality is the exposure.
Installation Design (co-location): elevator actuation and its monitoring wiring in the aft fuselage/empennage (zone 800). | A single zonal event could take both drive and monitor. | Rudder/elevator runs in zone 800 — confirm drive and monitor are separately routed.
Common Resources (hydraulic): elevators driven from HYD A and HYD C — dual-source. | Loss of one hydraulic source does not by itself cause a runaway; supports independence of the force path. | Dual hydraulic supply per SDD §5.3.2 supports the drive-side redundancy.
Development/Design (feedback sensing): shared position feedback between actuator loop and monitor. | Common sensor fault masks the runaway from the monitor. | Independence of the monitor's feedback source from the actuator's own loop must be shown.
cmaData.mitigation:
Require the FCC vote/monitor that arrests an uncommanded elevator runaway to use position/rate feedback and power independent of the actuator control electronics driving the surface, and confirm zonal separation of drive and monitor wiring in zone 800.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The runaway-arrest monitor for the elevator shall derive its detection from feedback and power independent of the actuator control electronics that command surface motion.
• Elevator actuation and its runaway-arrest monitoring wiring shall be separately routed such that no single zonal event disables both.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Each primary surface driven by at least two actuators on different hydraulic systems (elevators on A and C), with FCC vote/monitor arresting an uncommanded runaway.
aiRequirements: The runaway-arrest monitor for the elevator shall derive its detection from feedback and power independent of the actuator control electronics that command surface motion.
Elevator actuation and its runaway-arrest monitoring wiring shall be separately routed such that no single zonal event disables both.

cmaData.subject: G-006 independence: stabiliser trim runaway vs runaway monitor/cutout (uncommanded pitch motion)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the trim actuation/runaway source from the trim runaway monitor / cutout path.. Uncommanded stabiliser trim motion is arrested because runaway and the runaway monitor/cutout fail independently (AND gate, page-1788052528153-872 node 16).
cmaData.findings: Common Resources: SDD gives one all-moving trimmable stabiliser with a single trim actuator; runaway source and cutout monitor are not shown as physically diverse and may share the DC essential electrical supply and actuator control electronics. | Development/Design: common ACE / trim-control design between drive and monitor is a credible common-mode. | Installation: stabiliser trim actuation and mechanical reversion co-located in aft fuselage (zone 800). Common environment (thermal/EMI) in zone 800 can affect drive and cutout together.
cmaData.mitigation:
Require the trim runaway monitor / cutout to be powered and implemented independently of the trim drive (separate supply, dissimilar monitor). Require zonal separation of drive and cutout sensing in zone 800.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The stabiliser trim runaway cutout shall be electrically and functionally independent of the trim drive command path.
• The trim runaway monitor shall be substantiated as not sharing a common ACE design fault with the trim drive.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA to confirm as-built power segregation and dissimilarity of the cutout path; ZSA of zone 800 to confirm drive/cutout separation.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the trim actuation/runaway source from the trim runaway monitor / cutout path.
aiRequirements: The stabiliser trim runaway cutout shall be electrically and functionally independent of the trim drive command path.
The trim runaway monitor shall be substantiated as not sharing a common ACE design fault with the trim drive.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA to confirm as-built power segregation and dissimilarity of the cutout path; ZSA of zone 800 to confirm drive/cutout separation.

cmaData.subject: G-008 independence: three-way FCC vote of erroneous roll command
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the three flight control computers voting the roll command.. An erroneous roll command is not voted through because FCC channels 1/2/3 fail independently (AND gate, page-1788052528192-183 node 21).
cmaData.findings: Common Resources: shared air-data/inertial input feeds all three FCCs (a common corrupted air-data source can drive a coincident erroneous roll command); FCC3 (aft bay) is on the DC essential bus. | Development/Design: dissimilarity is only partial — three computers, software from two teams, so at least two channels share a software baseline (common software fault credible). | Installation: FCC1/FCC2/FCC3 are in three separate bays (zones 120/300/400), which supports physical independence. | Environment: separated bays reduce common thermal/EMI environment.
cmaData.mitigation:
Require independent/monitored air-data & inertial sourcing to the FCCs so a single source error cannot drive all three; require the two-team dissimilarity to guarantee no two voting channels share the same software item, or add cross-monitor coverage. Retain three-bay installation separation.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• No single air-data/inertial source error shall produce a coincident erroneous roll command across all three FCCs.
• The dissimilarity argument shall ensure the voting set does not depend on a single common software item.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm air-data source independence and the software dissimilarity allocation across the three FCCs; verify bay separation in ZSA.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the three flight control computers voting the roll command.
aiRequirements: No single air-data/inertial source error shall produce a coincident erroneous roll command across all three FCCs.
The dissimilarity argument shall ensure the voting set does not depend on a single common software item.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm air-data source independence and the software dissimilarity allocation across the three FCCs; verify bay separation in ZSA.

cmaData.subject: G-009 independence: erroneous roll command generation vs voting/monitor detection
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the erroneous-command generation from the voting/monitor that should detect and inhibit it.. An erroneous roll command does not reach the actuators because command generation and the voting/monitor detection fail independently (AND gate, page-1788052528192-183 node 20).
cmaData.findings: Development/Design: the voter/monitor executes inside the same FCC set that generates the roll command — a logical common-cause (a common FCC design or software fault can both generate the erroneous command and defeat its own detection). | Common Resources: shared air-data/inertial input and shared electrical supply to the FCC set couple generation and monitoring. | Installation: three-bay separation (zones 120/300/400) mitigates physical common-cause but not the shared-logic coupling.
cmaData.mitigation:
Require the cross-monitor/voter to be dissimilar from or independent of the command-generation logic (e.g. monitor on a diverse implementation) so a single design fault cannot both create and pass the erroneous command.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The roll-command voting/monitor shall not share a common design fault with the command-generation function it monitors.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA to confirm the voter/monitor's independence/dissimilarity from command generation; confirm no shared software item between generation and monitor.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the erroneous-command generation from the voting/monitor that should detect and inhibit it.
aiRequirements: The roll-command voting/monitor shall not share a common design fault with the command-generation function it monitors.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA to confirm the voter/monitor's independence/dissimilarity from command generation; confirm no shared software item between generation and monitor.

cmaData.subject: G-010 left aileron/spoiler group — HYD B left AND HYD C left actuator independence (page-1788052528192-183, node 27)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Fluid, pumping and distribution isolation between hydraulic systems B and C; separate actuators per surface.. The left roll surface tracks erroneously only if BOTH the HYD B left actuator and the HYD C left actuator independently produce erroneous tracking.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) Common actuator-control-electronics / FCC command to both left actuators | An erroneous command drives both actuators the same way, so the AND collapses to a single cause | FCS is 3 dissimilar FCCs voting with cross-monitor; ACE per surface is a shared node — treat FCC/ACE command as a repeated event above the two actuators
(2) Co-location of both left actuators at the same surface station | One local particular risk (uncontained rotor burst debris, tyre/tread fragment, zonal fire) strikes both actuators together | Actuators on one surface are necessarily co-located; reconcile against Rotor Burst (§25.903(d)(1)/AC 20-128A) and Tire Burst (§25.734) PRAs — physical separation cannot be claimed within one surface
(3) Shared hydraulic supply routing B and C at the wing root | If B and C shared a run, one zonal event drains both | Routings table: HYD C run (400,300,200) is routed separately from A/B (530,300,540) — B/C do NOT share the wing-root run; this supports the claim
(4) Common design/software in the two ACE lanes | A common logic/software defect produces identical erroneous tracking on both actuators | Dissimilarity is argued at FCC level (two teams); ACE-level dissimilarity not stated in SDD —
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain FCC/ACE command as an explicit repeated event above the two-actuator AND. Confirm B and C actuator control electronics are dissimilar or independently monitored. Reconcile actuator co-location with the Rotor Burst and Tire Burst PRAs. Development independence requirement: the two left-surface actuators shall not share a single control-electronics failure that commands both erroneously.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The left roll-surface actuation shall be arranged such that no single actuator-control-electronics or command failure causes both the HYD B and HYD C left actuators to track erroneously.
• The HYD B and HYD C left actuator supply routings shall maintain physical separation such that no single zonal event (rotor burst, tyre burst, zonal fire) disables both.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm: (a) B/C routing separation per §4 routings; (b) ACE independence/monitoring evidence; (c) PRA/ZSA disposition of co-located actuators against rotor-burst and tyre-burst debris.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Fluid, pumping and distribution isolation between hydraulic systems B and C; separate actuators per surface.
aiRequirements: The left roll-surface actuation shall be arranged such that no single actuator-control-electronics or command failure causes both the HYD B and HYD C left actuators to track erroneously.
The HYD B and HYD C left actuator supply routings shall maintain physical separation such that no single zonal event (rotor burst, tyre burst, zonal fire) disables both.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm: (a) B/C routing separation per §4 routings; (b) ACE independence/monitoring evidence; (c) PRA/ZSA disposition of co-located actuators against rotor-burst and tyre-burst debris.

cmaData.subject: G-011 right aileron/spoiler group — HYD B right AND HYD C right actuator independence (page-1788052528192-183, node 30)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Fluid, pumping and distribution isolation between hydraulic systems B and C; separate actuators per surface.. The right roll surface tracks erroneously only if BOTH the HYD B right actuator and the HYD C right actuator independently produce erroneous tracking.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) Common actuator-control-electronics / FCC command to both right actuators | An erroneous command drives both actuators together, collapsing the AND | 3 dissimilar voting FCCs; per-surface ACE is a shared node — model FCC/ACE command as a repeated event above the two actuators
(2) Co-location of both right actuators at the same surface station | A single local particular risk strikes both together | Reconcile against Rotor Burst (§25.903(d)(1)/AC 20-128A) and Tire Burst (§25.734) PRAs — no in-surface physical separation available
(3) Shared B/C hydraulic routing | One zonal event drains both supplies | HYD C run is routed separately from A/B per §4 — B/C do not share the wing-root run; supports the claim
(4) Common design/software in the two ACE lanes | Common defect produces identical erroneous tracking | FCC dissimilarity argued; ACE-level dissimilarity not stated —
cmaData.mitigation:
Mirror of G-010: retain FCC/ACE command as an explicit repeated event above the two-actuator AND; confirm B/C ACE dissimilarity or independent monitoring; reconcile actuator co-location with Rotor Burst and Tire Burst PRAs.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The right roll-surface actuation shall be arranged such that no single actuator-control-electronics or command failure causes both the HYD B and HYD C right actuators to track erroneously.
• The HYD B and HYD C right actuator supply routings shall maintain physical separation such that no single zonal event disables both.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm B/C routing separation, ACE independence evidence, and PRA/ZSA disposition of co-located actuators against rotor-burst and tyre-burst debris.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Fluid, pumping and distribution isolation between hydraulic systems B and C; separate actuators per surface.
aiRequirements: The right roll-surface actuation shall be arranged such that no single actuator-control-electronics or command failure causes both the HYD B and HYD C right actuators to track erroneously.
The HYD B and HYD C right actuator supply routings shall maintain physical separation such that no single zonal event disables both.

cmaData.subject: G-012 erroneous roll surface tracking — left group AND right group independence (page-1788052528192-183, node 26)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Left/right roll actuation independence; three isolated hydraulic systems.. Both roll groups track erroneously with a valid command only if the left group and the right group fail independently.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) HYD system C common to BOTH left and right roll surfaces | A single HYD C loss or erroneous-pressure event feeds an actuator in every roll surface, appearing in both AND branches | HYD C is a single system by design; model HYD C as a repeated event across the left and right branches — this partially defeats left/right independence
(2) Common voted FCC roll command to both sides | One erroneous voted command drives both groups the same way | 3 dissimilar FCCs voting with cross-monitor (node 20/21/25 model this above); ensure the voted-command failure is not double-counted as independent per side
(3) Common ADIRU / air-data source feeding the roll command | Corrupted reference drives both sides identically | Three reference units, two on main buses one on DC essential — cross-comparison monitor; represent shared reference as a common contributor
(4) Common FCC software across both sides | A common software defect corrupts both groups' commands | Dissimilarity argued between two software teams across three FCCs; residual common-mode of the voting/monitor logic — 
(5) Co-location — left/right groups on opposite wings | Genuine physical separation between sides | Left and right surfaces are on opposite semi-spans; a single localised event is unlikely to strike both — supports the claim
cmaData.mitigation:
Introduce HYD C as an explicit repeated event / common-cause gate spanning the left and right AND branches. Represent the voted FCC roll command and the shared air-data/inertial reference as common contributors above the left/right split rather than as independent per-side basic events. Development independence requirement: erroneous tracking of both roll groups shall not result from a single HYD C failure, a single voted-command failure, or a single reference-source error.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The roll-control architecture shall ensure that no single HYD system C failure causes both the left and right roll groups to track erroneously; HYD C shall be modelled as a repeated event across both branches.
• The voted FCC roll command and the shared air-data/inertial reference shall be represented as common contributors, not as independent per-side events, in the FC-003 fault tree.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm the fault tree carries HYD C as a repeated event and the voted-command/reference as common contributors; confirm FCC/software dissimilarity evidence supports the DAL-A independence argument underpinning FC-003.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Left/right roll actuation independence; three isolated hydraulic systems.
aiRequirements: The roll-control architecture shall ensure that no single HYD system C failure causes both the left and right roll groups to track erroneously; HYD C shall be modelled as a repeated event across both branches.
The voted FCC roll command and the shared air-data/inertial reference shall be represented as common contributors, not as independent per-side events, in the FC-003 fault tree.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm the fault tree carries HYD C as a repeated event and the voted-command/reference as common contributors; confirm FCC/software dissimilarity evidence supports the DAL-A independence argument underpinning FC-003.

cmaData.subject: G-015 AND-gate independence: uncommanded roll-surface drive vs FCC detect/inhibit monitor (FC-004)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between an actuator hazard-source and the FCC monitor arresting it, across common resources, common design and co-location.. The uncommanded roll-surface drive path and the FCC monitor that detects and inhibits it fail independently.

cmaData.subject: G-016 AND-gate independence: erroneous yaw command vs voter/cross-monitor rejection (FC-005)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between yaw command generation in the FCC voting complex and the cross-monitor/voter, across common design, software and common resources.. An erroneous yaw command and the voter/cross-monitor that rejects it fail independently.

cmaData.mitigation:
Verify the yaw cross-monitor/voter derives its comparison from a reference independent of the channel generating the command; confirm FCC dissimilarity covers monitor logic; confirm no single air-data/inertial source feeds both the command and its rejection basis.

• The yaw command voter/cross-monitor shall use a comparison reference independent of any single channel's command source.
• No single air-data or inertial reference failure shall simultaneously corrupt a yaw command and defeat its cross-monitor rejection.

cmaData.subject: G-022 AND-gate independence: pitch, roll, yaw and mechanical-reversion branches (FC-014)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence across three control axes and the mechanical reversion path, tested against shared hydraulic systems, shared FCC/EPS resources, common co-location and common environment.. Loss of pitch, loss of roll, loss of yaw and loss of the mechanical reversion path are independent, so complete loss of primary flight-path control requires all to fail together.
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence -- (Common Resources: hydraulics) Pitch uses HYD A+C, roll uses HYD B+C, yaw uses HYD A+B — HYD C is common to pitch and roll, HYD A common to pitch and yaw, HYD B common to roll and yaw | Loss of any two of A/B/C degrades two axis branches simultaneously, weakening the AND | SDD: three isolated circuits, PTU between A and B (fluid-isolated), RAT backstop to C — but the pairwise sharing means axis branches are not fully independent. -- (Installation Design: shared routing) HYD A and B share a wing-root run (530/300/540) | A zonal event in 530/300/540 could take A and B together, defeating both yaw (A+B) and one supply of pitch and roll | SDD records A/B wing-root run as an installation item for dedicated zonal attention — must be closed by ZSA/PRA. -- (Common Resources: FCC/EPS) Loss of FCC command appears in all three axis branches (nodes 52,56,60) | Common FCC/electrical failure could remove command to all surfaces at once | SDD: three FCCs on three sources — verify no single EPS or FCC failure collapses all three command branches. -- (Design diversity) Mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim and lower rudder only | Reversion is diverse from FBW and survives total FCC/electrical loss | SDD: reversion results from loss of all electrical command paths — verify reversion needs neither FCC nor the lost hydraulics for the credited axes. -- (Environment: particular risk) Rotor burst / engine debris (§25.903(d)(1)) or a zone-300 event could strike multiple hydraulic runs and FCC 2 co-located in mid hold | A single particular risk could defeat multiple axis branches | Reconcile with PRA (rotor/engine burst applicable) and ZSA for zones 300/530/540/800.
cmaData.mitigation:
Model HYD A, HYD B and HYD C as repeated/common-cause contributors across the axis branches rather than assuming full branch independence; add a common-cause gate for the A/B wing-root shared run; verify FCC/EPS command independence across axes; confirm mechanical reversion is free of FCC and of the shared hydraulic supplies for its credited surfaces; close against PRA (rotor/engine burst) and ZSA for zones 300/530/540/800.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• Loss of any single hydraulic system (A, B or C) shall not remove control of more than one control axis such that flight-path control is lost.
• A zonal event in the shared HYD A/B wing-root run (zones 530/300/540) shall not simultaneously defeat the yaw branch and the reversion path.
• The mechanical reversion path (stabiliser trim and lower rudder) shall require neither flight-control-computer command nor the hydraulic supplies whose loss it backstops.
• No single FCC or electrical-source failure shall remove flight-control command to all three control axes simultaneously.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm the top AND holds only after HYD A/B/C shared-supply couplings are represented as common-cause contributors; ZSA of zones 300/530/540/800 and PRA for uncontained rotor/engine burst to confirm no single particular risk collapses multiple axis branches; verify mechanical reversion independence.
