cmaData.subject: G-027 four-engine thrust independence — shared cross-feed gallery
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: The four engines' fuel supplies are independent so no single cause starves more than one engine.. Loss of thrust from all four engines arises only from independent per-engine causes (AND of four).
cmaData.findings: The cross-feed gallery is a SINGLE spanwise run through the wing box and is 'the only path by which fuel from one side reaches an engine on the other'; it transits zones 510/530/300/540/520. A single event on that run, or its mismanagement, can degrade fuel to engines on both sides, coupling the four otherwise-independent fuel feeds. This shared fuel path is a Common-Resource / Installation-Design common cause. Fuel exhaustion/mismanagement is already modelled explicitly (node 84) so is not double-counted; the residual concern is a physical event on the single gallery.
cmaData.mitigation:
Four isolation valves in the gallery; dedicated collector cell per engine kept full by adjacent-tank transfer; gravity feed path below FL150. Retained by the SDD as an item 'requiring particular-risk and zonal attention' — reconcile with the fuel-gallery PRA.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The fuel cross-feed gallery shall be isolatable such that a single physical breach or contamination event cannot starve engines on both sides simultaneously.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: The four engines' fuel supplies are independent so no single cause starves more than one engine.
aiRequirements: The fuel cross-feed gallery shall be isolatable such that a single physical breach or contamination event cannot starve engines on both sides simultaneously.

cmaData.subject: G-027 four-engine thrust independence — shared cross-bleed manifold and common engine/FADEC design
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: The four engines are independent in control and installation so no common design or shared service disables the set.. Loss of thrust from all four engines arises only from independent per-engine causes (AND of four).
cmaData.findings: All four engines are a single part number ('existing certified turbofan of the 330 kN class'); a common design/material deficiency is a Development/Design common cause across the redundant set. The four FADECs are of common design/software (dual-channel, cross-linked for data only) — a common software or specification error is a further Development common cause. High-pressure bleed is taken 'through a shared cross-bleed manifold' (zone 300) — a shared pneumatic resource, though bleed loss degrades ECS/IPS rather than directly stopping thrust. FADEC per-engine loss (nodes 69/73/77/81) is modelled explicitly; the common-design susceptibility across all four is the residual common-cause contributor.
cmaData.mitigation:
Four FADEC channels on four different power sources 'so that no single bus loss can affect more than one engine'; dual redundant channels per engine; in-service maturity of the selected type. Common part number 'recorded as a design-level installation item' (generators; same argument applies to the engine type).
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The common-design susceptibility of the four common-part-number engines and their common-design FADECs shall be substantiated (service history / dissimilarity argument) before crediting four-engine independence in the FC-034 tree.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: The four engines are independent in control and installation so no common design or shared service disables the set.
aiRequirements: The common-design susceptibility of the four common-part-number engines and their common-design FADECs shall be substantiated (service history / dissimilarity argument) before crediting four-engine independence in the FC-034 tree.

cmaData.subject: G-030 engine-2 inboard reverser inadvertent-deployment independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: The four inhibits on the engine-2 reverser fail independently so no single cause defeats them together.. Inadvertent in-flight deployment of the engine-2 reverser requires coincident failure of uncommanded deployment AND the WoW inhibit AND the RA-agreement inhibit AND the mechanical sleeve lock.
cmaData.findings: The WoW inhibit is driven by the LDG weight-on-wheels discrete, which the SDD lists as feeding 'a large number of consumers including the thrust reversers' — a Common-Resource coupling: a single erroneous WoW 'ground' signal simultaneously removes the WoW inhibit branch (node 88) at both inboard reversers, and is a shared cause between G-030 and G-031. The RA-agreement inhibit and the deployment/inhibit logic are of common design across the two inboard installations (Development/Design common cause). These couplings act across engines rather than within the single-engine AND.
cmaData.mitigation:
Deployment inhibited by WoW AND radio-altimeter agreement (two dissimilar inhibit criteria) PLUS a mechanical translating-sleeve lock; the mechanical lock is independent of the electrical inhibits. Reversers fitted to inboard engines only.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The weight-on-wheels signal used to inhibit reverser deployment shall be sourced/voted such that a single erroneous 'ground' indication cannot simultaneously enable both inboard reversers in flight.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: The four inhibits on the engine-2 reverser fail independently so no single cause defeats them together.
aiRequirements: The weight-on-wheels signal used to inhibit reverser deployment shall be sourced/voted such that a single erroneous 'ground' indication cannot simultaneously enable both inboard reversers in flight.

cmaData.subject: G-031 engine-3 inboard reverser inadvertent-deployment independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: The four inhibits on the engine-3 reverser fail independently so no single cause defeats them together.. Inadvertent in-flight deployment of the engine-3 reverser requires coincident failure of uncommanded deployment AND the WoW inhibit AND the RA-agreement inhibit AND the mechanical sleeve lock.
cmaData.findings: As for G-030: the WoW inhibit branch (node 93) draws on the shared LDG weight-on-wheels discrete that feeds the reversers, so a single erroneous WoW 'ground' signal is a Common-Resource cause shared between the engine-2 and engine-3 reverser inhibits. The radio-altimeter agreement inhibit and the uncommanded-deployment/inhibit logic are of common design across both inboard installations (Development/Design common cause). Engines 2 and 3 are in separate zones (620/630), so per-engine physical independence largely holds; the residual coupling is the shared inhibit source and common logic design.
cmaData.mitigation:
WoW AND radio-altimeter agreement inhibit plus an independent mechanical translating-sleeve lock; engine-3 installation is in a separate nacelle zone (630) from engine 2 (620).
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The reverser inhibit logic and inhibit-signal sources shall be shown to be free of a common cause capable of defeating both inboard reverser inhibits in the same flight.

aiRequirements: The reverser inhibit logic and inhibit-signal sources shall be shown to be free of a common cause capable of defeating both inboard reverser inhibits in the same flight.

cmaData.subject: G-033 (node 97) — independence of nose / left-main / right-main gear legs under FC-054
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Physical and functional separation of the three main-gear leg groups; retraction/extension supplied by HYD A with free-fall alternate.. The nose unit, left main bogies and right main bogies fail to support/absorb loads independently (AND).
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence :: (1) Shared HYD A retraction/extension supply to all legs [SDD 5.6.2 'Retraction and extension is by hydraulic system A'] | a single HYD A loss removes normal actuation to every leg simultaneously | free-fall alternate extension independent of hydraulic pressure is claimed as the mitigation, but that is the subject of G-034, not this gate :: (2) Common gear-leg design / single part-family across bogies | a common structural or material deficiency could affect multiple legs | preliminary leg/bogie count (SDD 1.2 'not frozen') — commonality to be substantiated :: (3) Co-location of left main / brake lines in zones 710/720 and nose in 730 — legs are in separate zones, which SUPPORTS independence for zonal threats | separate zones reduce single-event coupling | tire burst / flailing tread (§25.734, PRA on file) can strike a bogie group within one zone but not cross to the opposite side.
cmaData.mitigation:
Substantiate free-fall alternate independence from HYD A (covered by G-034). Confirm no common structural/material lot defeats multi-leg support. Preserve zonal separation of the three leg groups per zones 710/720/730.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The alternate gear-extension path shall be independent of hydraulic system A such that loss of HYD A does not defeat gear deployment.
• The three landing-gear leg groups shall be installed in separated zones such that no single zonal event disables more than one group.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Physical and functional separation of the three main-gear leg groups; retraction/extension supplied by HYD A with free-fall alternate.
aiRequirements: The alternate gear-extension path shall be independent of hydraulic system A such that loss of HYD A does not defeat gear deployment.
The three landing-gear leg groups shall be installed in separated zones such that no single zonal event disables more than one group.

cmaData.subject: G-034 (node 101) — independence of HYD A normal extension vs free-fall alternate extension under FC-054
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Free-fall alternate extension is independent of hydraulic pressure; uplocks/downlocks mechanically held, hydraulically released.. Normal extension (HYD A) and free-fall alternate extension fail independently (AND).
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence :: (1) Shared mechanical uplock/downlock hardware [SDD 5.6.2 'Uplocks and downlocks are mechanically held and hydraulically released'] | a mechanically jammed uplock defeats BOTH normal and free-fall paths — the release mechanism is common | free-fall relies on the same uplock releasing; independence limited to the motive source, not the release path :: (2) Common installation / rigging error at the gear bay | a single maintenance/rigging error could disable both extension paths | operating concept assumes 'no line maintenance capability at the strip' (SDD 1.1) — origin dispatch decision covers outbound+return :: (3) Shared gear-bay environment (zones 710/720/730, overheat detection fitted) | a single bay fire/overheat could seize the mechanism common to both paths | overheat detection fitted in main gear bays [SDD zone 710/720].
cmaData.mitigation:
Verify the free-fall path releases uplocks/downlocks by a means independent of the HYD A release actuation. Impose a rigging/installation independence requirement so a single error cannot disable both paths. Reconcile with the gear-bay ZSA.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The free-fall alternate extension shall release the gear uplocks by a mechanically independent means not shared with the hydraulic-release actuation.
• Installation and rigging procedures shall ensure a single maintenance error cannot disable both the normal and alternate gear-extension paths.

cmaData.subject: G-035 (node 106) — independence of the two downlock proximity sensing circuits under FC-054
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Downlock status sensed by two independent proximity circuits per unit.. Downlock proximity sensing circuit 1 and circuit 2 fail independently (AND).

SDD 5.7.2 dual DISSIMILAR sensing on the nose door — the gear circuits are stated 'independent' but dissimilarity is NOT claimed] | independence claimed but dissimilarity unstated for the gear proximity circuits — commonality to be examined :: (2) Co-location within the same gear bay (zones 710/720/730) | a single bay event (overheat, tire-burst debris) could affect both circuits | overheat detection fitted; tire-burst PRA on file — a flailing-tread strike could damage both harnesses if not separated :: (3) Shared electrical supply / signal route | a single supply or harness loss could take both circuits | separation of the two circuits' routing is not described in the SDD for the gear downlock sensing — to be confirmed.

Confirm the two downlock proximity circuits use dissimilar sensing and/or separated routing so a common type-defect or single bay event cannot disable both. Reconcile with the gear-bay ZSA and the tire-burst PRA.

cmaData.subject: G-036 independence: dual downlock proximity sensing (FC-054)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the two downlock proximity sensing circuits under the AND at node 106 (FC-054 fault tree).. The two independent downlock proximity sensing circuits per gear unit fail independently, so undetected loss of downlock integrity requires both to misread coincidentally.
cmaData.findings: VERIFICATION-phase (SSA/ASA). Concern: Common Resources — both proximity circuits are downlock position-sensing; SDD states 'two independent proximity circuits per unit' but does not describe supply diversity or physical routing separation, so shared DC supply / co-location cannot be excluded from the description. Concern: Installation Design / Environment — both circuits sit at the same downlock mechanism in the gear bay (zones 710/720/730), an unpressurised overheat-monitored fire-adjacent environment; a single localised event (heat, contamination, mechanical shock) at the lock can defeat both. Concern: Development/Design — 'identical in type' sensing is not asserted here but common part-number/design is not excluded. Concern: PRA — tire burst (§25.734) and gear-bay events strike within these zones. Excluded as not credible for this claim: shared network/data (proximity discretes), manufacturing lot (no data).
cmaData.mitigation:
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two downlock proximity sensing circuits per gear unit shall be supplied from independent electrical sources such that no single supply loss disables both.
• The two downlock proximity sensing circuits per gear unit shall be physically separated within the gear bay such that a single localised zonal event cannot defeat both.
Verification (SSA/ASA): Confirm in the LDG installation drawing that the two proximity circuits per unit use diverse supplies and separated routing; reconcile against the zone 710/720/730 ZSA before crediting the AND at node 106.

cmaData.subject: G-040 independence: primary display vs independent standby (FC-069)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the primary display path and the independent standby instrument under the AND at node 109 (FC-069 fault tree).. The primary display path and the independent standby instrument fail independently, so a misleading standby agreeing with a faulted primary requires two independent errors coinciding.
cmaData.findings: VERIFICATION-phase (SSA/ASA). Concern: Common Resources — SDD explicitly claims the standby 'shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays', which addresses electrical/sensor/processing commonality; residual exposure is that both derive attitude/airspeed/altitude from the SAME air mass and aircraft state, so a common external air-data environment (icing, blockage, unusual attitude) can bias both consistently. Concern: Common Resources (power) — standby is on DC essential; primary references include an ADIRU on DC essential, so DC-essential is a shared bus although the standby is a separate feed. Concern: Development/Design — both are attitude/air-data instruments; common algorithmic/design susceptibility to the same off-nominal air-data condition is not excluded. Concern: PRA — HIRF (§25.1317) / lightning (§25.1316) as a common electromagnetic environment reaching both. Excluded as not credible: shared processing/sensor (SDD explicitly denies), shared display feeder route (SDD states independent route).
cmaData.mitigation:
Standby instrument shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays; wired directly to DC essential on a route independent of the primary display feeders.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The primary display path and the standby instrument shall not be simultaneously corruptible by a single common air-data source error; a means to reveal a coincident consistent bias shall be provided.
Verification (SSA/ASA): Confirm the standby air-data/attitude sensing is physically and functionally independent of the primary pitot/static/AoA and ADIRU sensing; substantiate common-air-mass and HIRF/lightning common-environment coverage before crediting the AND at node 109.

cmaData.subject: G-043 independence: spurious unlock command vs pressure interlock (FC-078)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the spurious unlock command path and the ECS pressure interlock under the AND at node 125 (FC-078 fault tree).. A spurious/erroneous unlock command and the pressure interlock (residual differential <0.1 psi) fail independently, so an unlock reaches the actuator only if both the command is spurious and the interlock fails.
cmaData.findings: VERIFICATION-phase (SSA/ASA). Concern: Common Resources — the pressure interlock signal ('residual differential below 0.1 psi') is supplied by ECS, and both the door unlock command electronics and the interlock sensing may draw on shared EPS/DC-essential power and shared avionics/discrete paths (LDG weight-on-wheels, door logic); a common electrical source loss or corruption could both generate/permit a spurious command and defeat the interlock read. Concern: Installation Design — both interlock sensing and lock actuation are associated with the nose/forward-fuselage boundary (zones 110/120/130); co-location of command and interlock wiring is not excluded by the description. Concern: Development/Design — common software/logic in the door control that both issues the unlock and evaluates the interlock would be a single design fault defeating the AND. Excluded as not credible: mechanical latch/pin retention (separate from this command-vs-interlock claim; covered by node 118/122 logic), manufacturing lot (no data).
cmaData.mitigation:
Door cannot be opened with hold pressurised; a pressure interlock in series with the unlock command vents and confirms residual differential below 0.1 psi before the lock actuator will run.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The unlock command path and the ECS pressure interlock shall not share a single electrical source or processing element whose failure could both issue a spurious unlock and defeat the interlock.
• The pressure interlock evaluation shall be implemented independently of the door unlock command logic such that a single design fault cannot defeat both.
Verification (SSA/ASA): Confirm the ECS-supplied pressure interlock and the door unlock command derive from independent power sources and independent logic; reconcile against the NZD/ECS ICD before crediting the AND at node 125.

cmaData.subject: NZD nose-door uncommanded unlock — G-044 independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Latch and pin restraints on two separate hydraulic supplies, plus a pressure interlock in series with the unlock command, are independent barriers.. Pin restraint (8 pins) AND latch restraint (12 latches on common torque shaft) AND spurious-unlock-command path fail independently, so no single cause releases the door in flight.
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern: shared zone 110 (nose visor structure) housing latches, pins, lock actuator and sensing harness | Effect on the Principle: a particular-risk/zonal event confined to zone 110 can strike both the latch and pin restraints simultaneously, defeating the AND | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence: two hydraulic supplies (visor drive HYD A vs separate lock-pin actuator supply) give fluid-source separation but not zonal separation. --- Concern: twelve rotary latches driven by a COMMON torque shaft | Effect: a single torque-shaft failure disengages all twelve latches at once (not a redundant set) | Mitigating: eight independent locking pins driven separately are the retained barrier; this is design commonality within the latch branch, not across the AND. --- Concern: spurious/erroneous unlock command reaching actuators | Effect: an erroneous command could drive the lock actuator | Mitigating: ECS pressure interlock confirms residual differential below 0.1 psi before the actuator will run — a dissimilar, non-hydraulic barrier in series.
cmaData.mitigation:
Verify by installation review and zonal analysis that no single zone-110 event (impact, fire, structural) simultaneously defeats both latch and pin retention; confirm the pressure-interlock signal path shares no common cause with the unlock command path; confirm the common torque shaft failure is bounded by the eight-pin barrier.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA verification phase: close against as-built zone-110 installation evidence, PRA (nose visor impact/particular risk) and ZSA for zones 110/120/130.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Latch and pin restraints on two separate hydraulic supplies, plus a pressure interlock in series with the unlock command, are independent barriers.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA verification phase: close against as-built zone-110 installation evidence, PRA (nose visor impact/particular risk) and ZSA for zones 110/120/130.

cmaData.subject: NZD lock-indication independence — G-047
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Two dissimilar and independently routed lock-sensing circuits provide independent indication of lock state.. Proximity sensing harness (reads pin position) AND mechanical-linkage visual indicator fail independently, so both cannot misread 'locked' coincidentally.
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern: both sensing paths cross the flight-deck bulkhead at zone 110/120/130 boundary | Effect on the Principle: a common installation or maintenance error at the shared bulkhead crossing, or a zone-110 environment, could corrupt both paths and present a false 'locked' | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence: the two penetrations are stated as separated and the paths are dissimilar (electrical proximity vs mechanical linkage/visual), which counters common-mode failure but not a common installation/maintenance action. --- Concern: both paths sense the SAME physical pin/latch state | Effect: if the mechanical state itself is ambiguous (e.g. partial engagement), both may report the same wrong state — not a sensing common cause but a common measurand | Mitigating: dissimilar sensing method reduces coincident-error probability.
cmaData.mitigation:
Verify separated bulkhead penetrations and independent routing are maintained as built; confirm no shared maintenance/calibration action affects both the proximity harness and the mechanical indicator; confirm dissimilarity of the two sensing methods is preserved (no shared processing).
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA verification phase: close against as-built routing/penetration evidence and maintenance-task independence review; reconcile with ZSA for zones 110/120/130.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Two dissimilar and independently routed lock-sensing circuits provide independent indication of lock state.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA verification phase: close against as-built routing/penetration evidence and maintenance-task independence review; reconcile with ZSA for zones 110/120/130.

cmaData.subject: NZD visor-drive closure independence — G-048
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Visor is driven hydraulically from HYD A with an independent electric backup drive.. Hydraulic visor drive (HYD A) AND electric backup drive fail independently, so the door can always be driven to closed-and-locked.
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern: HYD A also supplies the visor drive AND is the retraction/extension/steering supply and the door actuation path | Effect on the Principle: loss of HYD A removes the primary drive, leaving only the electric backup; this is captured in the AND, but a common installation of HYD A and its electric-backup wiring in shared zone 110/forward fuselage could couple both | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence: the electric backup is a dissimilar power source (EPS vs HYD), which is the intended independence; verify their physical routing does not share a single zone-110 hazard. --- Concern: latch drive and lock-pin actuator closure steps depend on hydraulic/electric supplies that overlap the drive branch | Effect: a supply loss could prevent both drive AND lock completion | Mitigating: separate hydraulic supply for lock pins per §5.7.2.
cmaData.mitigation:
Verify HYD A drive and electric backup drive share no single-event zone; confirm the electric backup is fed from a bus not lost with HYD A's electrically-driven elements; confirm lock/latch drive supplies are separable from the visor-drive supply as built.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA verification phase: close against as-built EPS/HYD segregation evidence and zone-110/forward-fuselage ZSA.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Visor is driven hydraulically from HYD A with an independent electric backup drive.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA verification phase: close against as-built EPS/HYD segregation evidence and zone-110/forward-fuselage ZSA.

cmaData.subject: G-052 — Loss of latch AND pin retention in flight (nose pressure boundary, page-1788052528872-694, nodes 142/143/146)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the latch restraint path and the lock-pin restraint path of the nose cargo door.. The twelve-latch retention (common torque shaft) and the eight-pin retention (separate actuator, separate hydraulic supply) fail independently, so simultaneous loss of both restraints in flight requires two independent failures.
cmaData.findings:
VERIFICATION phase (supports ASA). Table M2 concerns tested against the SDD as-designed installation:
| Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence |
| Common Resources — hydraulic: latches on HYD A visor path; pins on a separate lock-actuator supply | If the two supplies are truly separate, no shared-hydraulic common cause | SDD §5.7.2: eight pins driven 'by a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply' — separation supports the claim |
| Installation Design — co-location: both latch and pin mechanisms housed in zone 110 (nose visor structure) | A single zonal event (structural distortion, impact) can defeat both restraints at once | Zone 110 houses 'visor latches, lock pins, lock actuator, sensing harness' together — co-location is a lack of independence |
| Development/Design — common torque shaft within the latch branch | Single mechanical element disengages all twelve latches (already a single point inside the latch branch, not across the AND) | §5.7.2 'Twelve rotary latches … driven by a common torque shaft'; pins block latch back-drive while engaged |
| Maintenance — common rigging/calibration action on latch and pin mechanisms during the same door service | A single erroneous maintenance action could compromise both restraints | Procedure not described in SDD — verification of independent maintenance tasks required |
| Environment — shared mechanical/thermal environment of the open/closed pressure boundary | Same environmental stress on both restraints | Pressure interlock confirms <0.1 psi before unlock — mitigates spurious unlock, not a shared structural cause |
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain the separate-hydraulic-supply separation between latch and pin actuation as an independence requirement; verify latch and pin mechanisms do not share a single maintenance rigging action; carry zone 110 co-location into the ZSA for the nose visor.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The latch drive and the lock-pin drive shall not share a hydraulic supply, actuator or control channel.
• Maintenance procedures for the twelve-latch and eight-pin mechanisms shall be independent tasks with independent verification.
Verification (SSA/ASA): Confirm via installation drawings and ICD that the pin actuator supply is physically and functionally separate from the HYD A visor drive; confirm maintenance task separation in the AMM; feed zone 110 co-location to the nose-visor ZSA.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the latch restraint path and the lock-pin restraint path of the nose cargo door.
aiRequirements: The latch drive and the lock-pin drive shall not share a hydraulic supply, actuator or control channel.
Maintenance procedures for the twelve-latch and eight-pin mechanisms shall be independent tasks with independent verification.
cmaData.aiVerification: Confirm via installation drawings and ICD that the pin actuator supply is physically and functionally separate from the HYD A visor drive; confirm maintenance task separation in the AMM; feed zone 110 co-location to the nose-visor ZSA.

cmaData.subject: G-054 — Loss of electrical supply to all heated probes, ports and windshields (page-1788052528946-68, nodes 150/151/152/153)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the AC-supply, DC-supply and heater-control paths feeding the heated air-data elements.. Loss of AC supply, loss of DC supply and loss of heater control to the heated elements are independent, so complete loss of probe/port/windshield heating requires the coincidence of independent electrical failures.
cmaData.findings:
VERIFICATION phase (supports ASA). Table M2 concerns tested against the SDD:
| Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence |
| Common Resources — electrical: heated elements drawn from the EPS resource that supplies all systems | AC and DC feeds both trace to the same four-generator EPS; a common upstream generation/distribution loss couples the AC and DC branches | §5.5 EPS 'generates … distributes power to every consumer'; §5.10.2 probes/windshields 'electrically heated' — shared source is a lack of independence |
| Common Resources — DC essential dependency | If both DC feed and heater control sit on the DC essential path, one bus event defeats two AND inputs | §5.5.2 DC essential is 'the aircraft's final electrical resort' feeding many critical loads — verify heater feeds are not commonly essential-bus dependent |
| Development/Design — common heater-control design/software across elements | A common controller design fault removes control to all elements simultaneously | §5.10.2 elements 'monitored individually'; controller commonality not resolved in SDD |
| Environment — shared harsh external icing/thermal environment at the sensing locations | Same environmental cause can degrade multiple heated elements | Elements are physically distributed (probes/ports/windshields) — partial mitigation |
cmaData.mitigation:
Verify AC and DC feeds to the heated elements do not converge on a single bus or feeder; confirm heater-control channels are not a single common design/software item; carry the EPS-as-shared-resource coupling to CMA at EPS level.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The AC supply, DC supply and heater-control channel to the heated air-data elements shall not share a single bus, feeder or common controller.
• Heater-control functions shall be substantiated as free of a common design/software fault that removes control to all elements simultaneously.
Verification (SSA/ASA): Trace AC/DC feeders and heater-control allocation on the EPS/EWS routing to confirm no single-bus or single-controller convergence; confirm dissimilarity or independence of heater-control channels.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the AC-supply, DC-supply and heater-control paths feeding the heated air-data elements.
aiRequirements: The AC supply, DC supply and heater-control channel to the heated air-data elements shall not share a single bus, feeder or common controller.
Heater-control functions shall be substantiated as free of a common design/software fault that removes control to all elements simultaneously.
cmaData.aiVerification: Trace AC/DC feeders and heater-control allocation on the EPS/EWS routing to confirm no single-bus or single-controller convergence; confirm dissimilarity or independence of heater-control channels.

cmaData.subject: G-058 — Detection fails to signal the actual fire/overheat in the aft zone (FC-099, page-1788052528988-327, nodes 155/156/159 with 162/163/164/165)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between fire-detection loop 1 and fire-detection loop 2 (and the loop-fault annunciation path) in the aft/APU fire zone.. Dual continuous detection loops routed separately (AND logic for warning) fail independently, so failure to signal an actual aft-zone fire requires both loops to fail together, plus a failure to annunciate the loop fault.
cmaData.findings:
VERIFICATION phase (supports ASA). Table M2 concerns tested against the SDD:
| Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence |
| Development/Design — identical loop type: both loops are the same continuous-detection design | A common design/material deficiency (a susceptible characteristic per NASA-FTH for identical redundant elements) defeats both loops together | §5.12.2 'dual-loop continuous fire detection, with the two loops routed separately' — separate routing mitigates physical, not design, common cause |
| Common Resources — electrical: DC essential supply to FPR detection (node 165) | Loss of DC essential removes both loops and the annunciation path at once | §5.12.4 'DC power from the essential bus to detection'; node 165 already models this — a genuine shared-resource common cause |
| Installation Design — co-location: both loops within the aft-fuselage/APU fire zone (zone 800) | The very fire the loops must detect, or an APU-compartment event, can damage both loops before they signal | Loops 'routed on opposite sides of that zone and separately clipped' — separation reduces but does not eliminate shared-zone exposure |
| Environment — shared thermal/vibration environment of zone 800 (mixed, APU fire zone) | Common environmental stress on identical sensing elements | Opposite-side routing is the mitigating factor; no dissimilarity of loop type |
cmaData.mitigation:
Model the identical-loop common-design cause and the DC-essential shared supply explicitly as common-cause contributors under the detection AND (repeated event or dedicated CCF gate); verify opposite-side routing and separate clipping in zone 800; carry to the zone 800 ZSA and APU fire particular-risk work.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• A common-cause contributor for the two identical detection loops (common design and shared DC-essential supply) shall be represented explicitly under the detection AND gate.
• Detection loops 1 and 2 in zone 800 shall be verified as separately routed and clipped such that a single zonal event does not disable both before signalling.
Verification (SSA/ASA): Confirm loop routing separation and clipping in zone 800 against installation drawings; confirm the loop-fault/BITE monitor annunciates a single-loop loss so degraded single-loop logic is crew-known; add the identical-loop CCF contributor to the fault tree.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between fire-detection loop 1 and fire-detection loop 2 (and the loop-fault annunciation path) in the aft/APU fire zone.
aiRequirements: A common-cause contributor for the two identical detection loops (common design and shared DC-essential supply) shall be represented explicitly under the detection AND gate.
Detection loops 1 and 2 in zone 800 shall be verified as separately routed and clipped such that a single zonal event does not disable both before signalling.
cmaData.aiVerification: Confirm loop routing separation and clipping in zone 800 against installation drawings; confirm the loop-fault/BITE monitor annunciates a single-loop loss so degraded single-loop logic is crew-known; add the identical-loop CCF contributor to the fault tree.

cmaData.subject: FC-099 detection AND annunciation independence (G-060, page-1788052528988-327 node 154)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Dual-loop continuous detection (loops routed separately, AND logic degrading to single-loop) combined with an independent loop-fault BITE/annunciation path to the crew.. The two fire/overheat detection loops fail independently AND the annunciation path is independent of the detection failure, so an undetected failure-to-warn requires both branches to fail.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources: DC essential bus supplies FPR detection AND the loop-fault monitor/BITE — a single DC-ess loss defeats detection response and the fault annunciation together (already a repeated event, node 165 'DC essential supply loss to FPR detection', combined at the top AND). Installation-Design/Environment: the two loops are co-located within the same nacelle/APU fire zone (610/620/630/640/800); a fire severe enough to be the condition being detected can damage both loops before either signals — the initiating hazard and the common environment coincide. Development/Design: both loops are continuous-detection elements of the same type, a common design/technology susceptibility. Common Resources: the crew-alerting path (node 164) is shared consolidated alerting (SF-010) — a loss of consolidated alerting silences the warning regardless of detection state. Table M2 — Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence: (1) DC essential supply | disables detection response and BITE annunciation together | loops/BITE not independent of DC-ess — modelled as repeated event, but is it truly common? verify supply topology; (2) Same-zone co-location of both loops in the fire zone | the fire being detected can disable both before warning | separate routing/clipping on opposite sides of the zone per SDD 5.12.5 — verify separation withstands the fire it must detect; (3) Identical loop type/technology | common design deficiency defeats both loops | dissimilarity not claimed — records identical loops; (4) Shared consolidated alerting channel | valid warning not presented to crew | dual independent alerting channels claimed (SF-010) — verify the FPR alert traverses both.
cmaData.mitigation: Confirm the DC essential dependency is genuinely common (single feed) or split detection vs. annunciation supply; verify loop separation/fire-hardening is qualified against the fire the loops must detect; substantiate that identical-type loops do not share a design/environmental failure mode; verify the FPR warning reaches the crew over both independent alerting channels.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Dual-loop continuous detection (loops routed separately, AND logic degrading to single-loop) combined with an independent loop-fault BITE/annunciation path to the crew.

cmaData.subject: FC-122 generation AND monitor independence (G-065, page-1788052529059-75 node 166)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Cross-comparison monitoring across independent reference sources plus independent alerting, gating an erroneous display so it cannot go undetected.. Erroneous flight-information generation is independent of the cross-comparison monitor that would flag it, so undetected misleading flight information requires both the generation error and a monitor failure.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources (sensors/data): common pitot/static/AoA sensing (node 170) and common ADIRU behaviour can corrupt the value displayed AND the comparands the monitor uses — a source error that is common to all references defeats cross-comparison (the monitor cannot flag an error present identically in every input). Common Resources (processing/network): display processing (node 172) and the deterministic data network (node 173) are shared between the presented data and, potentially, the monitor's inputs — a corrupt network channel can both mispresent and starve the monitor. Development/Design: the three ADIRUs are same-type reference units; a common design fault produces coincident, agreeing errors that the cross-comparison passes as valid. Common Resources (electrical): two ADIRUs on the main buses and one on DC essential (SDD 5.11.2) — verify the monitor is not co-supplied with the sources it checks. Table M2 — Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor / Lack of Independence: (1) Common pitot/static/AoA sensing feeding all references | identical error in every comparand — monitor sees agreement | air-data source diversity/heating separation — verify probe/port independence (ties to FC-089 undetected probe-heating loss); (2) Shared display processing / data network | mispresentation and monitor input corrupted together | dual networks on opposite sides, no shared connector (SDD 5.11.5) — verify monitor draws from the independent channel; (3) Same-type ADIRUs | coincident agreeing errors pass cross-comparison | three units, one on DC-ess — dissimilarity of reference units not claimed; (4) Alerting channel | flagged discrepancy not annunciated | dual independent alerting channels — verify the discrepancy alert traverses both.
cmaData.mitigation: Verify the cross-comparison monitor uses sources/comparands independent of the display-generation path (independent sensing, independent network channel, independent supply); substantiate that common pitot/static/AoA sensing errors are detectable by a means other than reference-to-reference comparison; confirm same-type ADIRUs do not produce common-mode agreeing errors; verify the annunciation reaches the crew over both alerting channels.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Cross-comparison monitoring across independent reference sources plus independent alerting, gating an erroneous display so it cannot go undetected.

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detect the erroneous pitch response as a mismatch between their pitch inceptor input and the aircraft attitude and pitch cues, identify it as an erroneous surface response rather than a valid one, and apply corrective pitch input to recover the flight path.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-001 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detect the uncommanded pitch motion from the attitude and pitch cues absent any pitch input, identify it as an uncommanded surface motion, and apply and hold counter pitch input to arrest the excursion.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-002 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detect the erroneous roll response as a mismatch between their roll inceptor input and the bank cues, identify it as an erroneous surface response rather than a valid one, and apply corrective roll input to recover the flight path.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-003 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detect the uncommanded roll motion from the bank and roll-rate cues absent any roll input, identify it as an uncommanded surface motion, and apply and hold counter roll input to arrest the excursion.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-004 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detect the erroneous yaw response as a mismatch between their pedal input and the yaw and sideslip cues, identify it as an erroneous surface response rather than a valid one, and apply corrective pedal input to recover.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-005 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew perceive the yaw excursion from the yaw and sideslip cues, apply and hold corrective pedal input, and identify and isolate the affected rudder segment while managing the dynamic upset.

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detect the restricted control authority as a surface jam from control response and jam discretes, diagnose the affected axis and available paths, revert to the remaining control paths, and fly a degraded-control landing.

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew, who are unaware of the sub-threshold pitch drift, would detect it only if it eventually produces a perceptible attitude or performance change on the attitude and performance displays.

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew, who are unaware of the sub-threshold roll drift, would detect it only if it eventually produces a perceptible bank or heading change on the attitude and heading displays.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-009 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew, who are unaware of the sub-threshold yaw drift, would detect it only if it eventually produces a perceptible yaw, sideslip or lateral-trim change on the flight cues.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-010 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew carry the additional load of maintaining pitch attitude and trim through the remaining pitch means, recognising the degraded-law annunciation where the control law degrades.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-011 · framed per HIDH §5.7 cognitive workload

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew carry the additional load of maintaining wings level and lateral flight path through the remaining roll means, recognising the degraded-law annunciation where the control law degrades.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-012 · framed per HIDH §5.7 cognitive workload

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew carry the additional load of maintaining directional control through the remaining yaw means, most demanding when coincident with asymmetric outboard thrust, recognising the degraded-law annunciation where applicable.

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew perceive the thrust or aircraft response as inconsistent with lever position, diagnose the affected engine, manage it via fuel shut-off or fire handle, and counter any resulting asymmetry with rudder.

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew observe the unexpected thrust or speed change on the engine indications, identify the affected engine, disconnect autothrottle and manage the engine via fuel shut-off or fire handle while countering the asymmetry.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from FC-028 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detect the thrust asymmetry from the yaw and engine cues, apply and hold corrective rudder, and manage the offending engine, with directional control governing at low speed and high thrust.

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew, who are unaware of the sub-threshold thrust drift, would detect it only if it grows past a detection threshold or manifests through a secondary speed or heading trend cue.

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew, who are unaware of the actual thrust error because the thrust indication is false, manage thrust to the false indication and take no corrective action, discovering the error only late through a secondary cue.
